1:1.headline: A place called Tofel hints at complaints about the manna
1:1.body: No place named Tofel and Lavan appears anywhere else. Rashi reads them as hints: תפל sounds like 'they spoke slightingly', and לבן means 'white', the color of the manna. Rashbam says they are simply place names.

sources.quote: חזרנו על כל המקרא ולא מצינו מקום ששמו תפל ולבן, אלא הוכיחן על הדברים שתפלו על המן, שהוא לבן
sources.says: Rashi quotes Rabbi Yochanan: no such place exists, so Moses was rebuking them for speaking slightingly of the manna, which is white.

sources.quote: הכל מקומות לפי פשוטו
sources.says: Rashbam says that by the plain meaning these are all just places.

1:1.headline: Di Zahav, 'enough gold', points to the golden calf
1:1.body: The place name די זהב means something like 'plenty of gold'. Rashi hears in it a rebuke for the golden calf, made because they had so much gold. Rashbam says it is a place name, like the personal name Mei Zahav.

sources.quote: הוכיחן על העגל שעשו בשביל רב זהב שהיה להם
sources.says: Rashi says Moses rebuked them for the calf they made because of all the gold they had.

sources.quote: כמו: בת מי זהב שהוא שם
sources.says: Rashbam compares it to the name 'daughter of Mei Zahav' and says it is a name.

1:5.headline: Moses explained the Torah in seventy languages
1:5.body: The verb באר means 'make clear'. Rashi, citing the midrash, says Moses made it clear by putting it into seventy languages.

sources.quote: בשבעים לשון פרשה להם
sources.says: Rashi says Moses explained the Torah to them in seventy languages.

1:10.headline: 'You are today like the stars' becomes 'you are like the day'
1:10.body: Israel was not literally as many as the stars that day. So Rashi reads היום, 'today', as 'like the day': lasting forever like the sun, moon and stars.

sources.quote: הנכם משולים כיום – קימים לעולם כחמה וכלבנה וככוכבים
sources.says: Rashi says it means you are compared to the day, lasting forever like the sun, moon and stars.

1:12.headline: Moses' 'how can I' is the first of three laments
1:12.body: איכה, 'how', is the word that opens the book of Lamentations. The midrash says three prophets spoke with this word: Moses here, then Isaiah and Jeremiah. Moses said it when Israel was at its height.

sources.quote: שלשה נתנבאו בלשון איכה, משה, ישעיה, וירמיה
sources.says: The midrash says three prophets prophesied using the word איכה: Moses, Isaiah and Jeremiah.

sources.quote: משה ראה את ישראל בכבודם ושלותם ואמר: איכה אשא לבדי טרחכם
sources.says: It says Moses saw Israel in their honor and calm and said 'how can I bear your burden alone'.

1:12.headline: Your 'trouble': endless lawsuits, or the work of teaching you
1:12.body: Rashi says טרחכם means the people were troublesome in court, always bringing more witnesses. Ibn Ezra and Ramban say it is the hard work of teaching the laws to simple people.

sources.quote: מלמד שהיו ישראל טרחנין
sources.says: Rashi says it teaches that Israel were troublesome people who dragged out cases.

sources.quote: טרחכם להבין אנשים פתאים המצות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is the trouble of making simple people understand the commandments.

sources.quote: כי טרח גדול היה ללמד ליוצאי מצרים החקים והתורת
sources.says: Ramban says it was a great burden to teach the laws to those who left Egypt.

1:12.headline: Your 'load': suspicious grumblers, demands for food, or prayer
1:12.body: משא means a load. Rashi says the load was people who suspected Moses of plotting. Ibn Ezra says it was their demands for bread, water and meat. Ramban reads it as prayer, from the phrase 'lift up a prayer'.

sources.quote: מלמד שהיו אפיקורסין
sources.says: Rashi says it teaches that they were scoffers who read bad motives into whatever Moses did.

sources.quote: שבקשו לחם ומים ובשר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means they asked for bread, water and meat.

sources.quote: שהוא ענין תפלה שמתפלל עליהם, והוא מלשון ונשאת תפלה
sources.says: Ramban says it is the prayer Moses prayed for them, from the phrase 'and lift up a prayer'.

1:13.headline: What makes a person נבון, not just wise
1:13.body: Rashi says a נבון understands one thing from another. He tells of a money changer who goes out and finds work, while the merely wise one waits. Two verses later Moses found wise men, but no נבונים.

sources.quote: מבינים דבר מתוך דבר
sources.says: Rashi says נבונים are people who understand one thing from another.

sources.quote: נבון דומה לשלחני תגר, כשמביאין לו מעות לראות רואה, וכשאין מביאין לו, הוא מחזר ומביא משלו
sources.says: Rashi says the נבון is like a trading money changer who, when no one brings him coins, goes and brings his own.

sources.quote: אבל נבונים לא מצאתי
sources.says: Rashi says that when Moses chose judges, he did not find any נבונים.

1:13.headline: Rashi reads 'I will set them' as spelled like 'their guilt'
1:13.body: Rashi read this word without a yod, as ואשמם. Spelled that way it looks like אשם, 'guilt'. He says the people's guilt hangs on their judges, who should have stopped them.

sources.quote: שאשמותיהם של ישראל תלויות בראשי דיניהם
sources.says: Rashi says the guilt of Israel hangs on the heads of their judges.

sources.quote: ואשמם חסר יו״‎ד ה״‎ג בפרש״‎י
sources.says: Chizkuni says the right text of Rashi reads the word as ואשמם, missing a yod.

1:16.headline: גרו: a stranger, a legal opponent, or a neighbor
1:16.body: גרו usually means 'his stranger'. Rashi gives two other readings. It is his opponent, who piles up (אוגר) claims against him. Or it is about where people live, even a dispute over an oven.

sources.quote: זה בעל דינו שאוגר עליו דברים
sources.says: Rashi says it is his opponent in court, who piles up words against him.

sources.quote: אף על עסקי דירה בין חלקת אחים, אפלו בין תנור לכירים
sources.says: Rashi also reads it as disputes about dwelling, even between brothers dividing an oven and a stove.

1:17.headline: Do not fear anyone, or do not hold back your words
1:17.body: Rashi gives two readings of תגורו. The first is 'do not be afraid'. The second comes from אגר, 'gather in', as in Proverbs: do not hold your words back because of anyone.

sources.quote: לא תכניס דבריך מפני איש, לשון "אגר בקיץ"
sources.says: Rashi says it can mean do not hold in your words because of any man, from 'gathers in summer'.

1:24.headline: The Eshkol valley is called by a name it had not yet earned
1:24.body: אשכל means a cluster of grapes. In Numbers 13 the valley gets this name because the spies cut a cluster there. Rashi says the verse calls it by the name it would have later.

sources.quote: מגיד שנקרא על שם סופו
sources.says: Rashi says it shows the place is called by the name of what happened later.

1:42.headline: Going up the mountain would bring them down
1:42.body: עלה means to climb, and also to rise in standing. Rashi plays on both: going up would not be a rise for them but a fall. Maimonides lists rising in status as a second sense of עלה.

sources.quote: לא עליה תהא לכם אלא ירידה
sources.says: Rashi says it will not be a going up for you, but a going down.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 1, Chapter 10
sources.quote: לאחר מכן הושאלו המונחים הללו לרוממות ולגדולה
sources.says: Maimonides says the words for going up and down were later borrowed for rise and fall in greatness.

1:44.headline: The Amorites chased them like bees, and paid for it
1:44.body: Rashi says a bee dies once it stings, and so the attackers died as soon as they struck. Ibn Ezra reads the image plainly: bees chase anyone who touches their hive.

sources.quote: מה הדבורה הזאת כשהיא מכה את האדם מיד מתה
sources.says: Rashi says that just as a bee dies as soon as it stings a person, so did the attackers.

sources.quote: כי מי שיגע אל ביתם מיד ירדפו אחריו וינשכוהו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says whoever touches their nest, bees chase at once and sting.

1:46.headline: Same letters, two verbs: they returned, then they stayed
1:46.body: In verse 45 ותשבו means 'you returned' and wept. In verse 46 the same letters mean 'you stayed' in Kadesh a long time. Onkelos uses two different words. Maimonides says ישב also means staying fixed in place.

sources.quote: ותבתון ובכיתון קדם יי
sources.says: Onkelos translates verse 45 as 'you returned and wept before the Lord'.

sources.quote: ויתבתון ברקם יומין סגיאין
sources.says: Onkelos translates verse 46 as 'you sat in Rekem many days'.

sources.quote: ותשבו לשון עכבה
sources.says: Chizkuni says ותשבו here means staying put.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 1, Chapter 11
sources.quote: הושאל המונח לכל מצב יציב וקבוע שאינו משתנה
sources.says: Maimonides says sitting was borrowed to mean any fixed state that does not change.

10:12.headline: "What does God ask of you?" Read מה as מאה: a hundred blessings
10:12.body: Moses asks מה, "what", does God ask of you. The Talmud learns from this verse that a person should say a hundred blessings a day. Rashi explains: read מה as מאה, "a hundred". Rabbeinu Bahya adds that the verse has 99 letters, and adding the א makes 100.

sources.quote: חַיָּיב אָדָם לְבָרֵךְ מֵאָה בְּרָכוֹת בְּכׇל יוֹם
sources.says: Rabbi Meir says a person must say a hundred blessings every day, citing this verse.

sources.quote: מה ה' אלהיך וגו' - קרי ביה מאה
sources.says: Rashi says to read the word מה as מאה, a hundred.

sources.quote: ויש בפסוק זה צ"ט אותיות ועם אל"ף שתשים במלת מ"ה ישלמו למאה אותיות
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says the verse has 99 letters, and with an א added to מה there are 100.

10:16.headline: "The foreskin of your heart" is what blocks it
10:16.body: Moses says to circumcise the ערלה, "foreskin", of the heart. Rashi says it means the heart's blockage and covering. Onkelos translates "remove the dullness of your heart", and Ramban says the heart should be open to know the truth.

sources.quote: אֹטֶם לְבַבְכֶם וְכִסּוּיוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means the blockage and covering of your heart.

sources.quote: וְתֶעְדּוּן יָת טַפְשׁוּת לִבְּכוֹן
sources.says: Onkelos translates "remove the dullness of your heart".

sources.quote: שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְבַבְכֶם פָּתוּחַ לָדַעַת הָאֱמֶת
sources.says: Ramban says it means your heart should be open to know the truth.

10:17.headline: "God of the elohim": of judges, or of angels
10:17.body: God is called אלהי האלהים, "God of the elohim". Onkelos reads elohim here as judges: "God of judges and Lord of kings". Rabbeinu Bahya reads it as the angels.

sources.quote: אֱלָהָא דַּיָּנִין וּמָרֵי מַלְכִין
sources.says: Onkelos translates "God of judges and Lord of kings".

sources.quote: הוא אלהי האלהים. המלאכים
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says the elohim here are the angels.

10:17.headline: God takes no "bribe": a good deed does not cancel a sin
10:17.body: God "takes no bribe". Sforno and Rabbeinu Bahya say the bribe is a good deed offered against a sin. God does not let one cancel the other. He punishes the sin and rewards the good deeds separately.

sources.quote: לֹא יָסִיר כְּלָל מֵעֹנֶשׁ הָעֲבֵרָה בִּשְׁבִיל זְכוּת מִצְוָה שֶׁעָשָה הַחוֹטֵא
sources.says: Sforno says God does not remove the punishment for a sin because of a good deed the sinner did.

sources.quote: אלא הוא מענישו על אותה עבירה יחידית ונותן לו שכר על רבוי המצות כלן
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says God punishes the single sin and still rewards all the many good deeds.

10:20.headline: The small word את: fear God, and also respect the wise
10:20.body: A sage read meaning into every את, a small word that marks the object. When he reached "את God you shall fear", he stopped. Rabbi Akiva later read this one too: it includes Torah scholars.

sources.quote: הָיָה דּוֹרֵשׁ כׇּל ׳אֶתִּים׳ שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְ״אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ תִּירָא״ פֵּירַשׁ
sources.says: The Talmud says Shimon HaAmsoni explained every את in the Torah, but when he reached this verse he stopped.

sources.quote: עַד שֶׁבָּא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְדָרַשׁ: ״אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ תִּירָא״ — לְרַבּוֹת תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
sources.says: Rabbi Akiva then taught that this את includes Torah scholars.

11:6.headline: היקום: the wealth that keeps a person standing
11:6.body: The earth swallowed Dathan and Abiram with כל היקום, "everything that stood" at their feet. Rashi hears the root "to stand": it is a person's money, which keeps him on his feet. Ibn Ezra reads it simply as everything that existed.

sources.quote: זֶה מָמוֹנוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם שֶׁמַּעֲמִידוֹ עַל רַגְלָיו
sources.says: Rashi says this is a person's money, which stands him on his feet.

sources.quote: ואת כל היקום. שם כלל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says היקום is a general word for everything.

11:10.headline: Watering "with your foot": Egypt made you work for water
11:10.body: Egypt is a land you water "with your foot". Rashi explains: there you had to haul water from the Nile on foot and lose sleep over it. In Israel the rain waters every field while you sleep.

sources.quote: צָרִיךְ אַתָּה לִנְדֹּד מִשְּׁנָתְךָ וְלַעֲמֹל
sources.says: Rashi says in Egypt you had to bring water from the Nile on foot, losing sleep and toiling.

sources.quote: אַתָּה יָשֵׁן עַל מִטָּתְךָ וְהַקָּבָּ"ה מַשְׁקֶה
sources.says: Rashi says in Israel you sleep in your bed while God waters the land.

11:12.headline: "From the beginning of the year", spelled without its א
11:12.body: The word מרשית, "from the beginning", is written without its usual א. Rabbeinu Bahya sees in this a hint to Tishrei, the month of the new year. Rashi says that at the start of the year it is decided what will happen at its end.

sources.quote: חסר אל"ף, ויהיה הרמז לחדש תשרי שהוא ראש השנה לבריאתו של עולם
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says the missing א hints at the month of Tishrei, the new year of the world's creation.

sources.quote: מֵרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה נִדּוֹן מַה יְּהֵא בְּסוֹפָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says at the start of the year it is judged what will be at its end.

11:13.headline: "If you listen, you will listen": hold on to the old, gain the new
11:13.body: The verse doubles the verb: שמע תשמעו, "listening you will listen". Rashi reads the doubling as a promise: if you keep listening to what you already learned, you will come to hear new things.

sources.quote: אִם שָׁמֹעַ בַּיָּשָׁן תִּשְׁמְעוּ בֶּחָדָשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says: if you listen to the old, you will hear the new.

11:13.headline: "Serve Him with your heart": the service of the heart is prayer
11:13.body: עבודה usually means work or the Temple service. But here it is service "with all your heart". Rashi says the service done in the heart is prayer.

sources.quote: עֲבוֹדָה שֶׁהִיא בַּלֵּב, וְזוֹ הִיא תְפִלָּה
sources.says: Rashi says it is service that is in the heart, and that is prayer.

sources.quote: איזוהי עבודה שבלב הוי אומר זו תפלה
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya cites the sages: what is service of the heart? It is prayer.

11:14.headline: The first rain, יורה, "teaches" people to patch their roofs
11:14.body: יורה is the early autumn rain. The Talmud hears the verb "to teach" in it: the first rain teaches people to plaster their roofs and bring in their crops. Ibn Ezra hears "to show": it shows that a good year is coming.

sources.quote: שֶׁמּוֹרֶה אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת לְהָטִיחַ גַּגּוֹתֵיהֶן
sources.says: The Talmud says the rain is called יורה because it teaches people to plaster their roofs.

sources.quote: גשם שיורה על שנה טובה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is rain that shows a good year is coming.

sources.quote: הִיא רְבִיעָה הַנּוֹפֶלֶת לְאַחַר הַזְּרִיעָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is the rain that falls after sowing and soaks the land.

11:14.headline: The late rain: "late", "on the stalks", or "cutting away hardness"
11:14.body: מלקוש is the spring rain. Rashi gives two readings: "late", or rain that falls on the ears and stalks (מלילות, קשין). The Talmud adds a third: rain that "circumcises" (מל) Israel's hardness (קשיות).

sources.quote: וּלְשׁוֹן מַלְקוֹשׁ דָּבָר הַמְאֻחָר
sources.says: Rashi says the word means something late.

sources.quote: שֶׁיּוֹרֶדֶת עַל הַמְּלִילוֹת וְעַל הַקַּשִּׁין
sources.says: Rashi gives another reading: it falls on the ears of grain and the stalks.

sources.quote: דָּבָר שֶׁמָּל קַשְׁיוּתֵיהֶן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Shmuel says it is something that cuts away Israel's hardness.

11:16.headline: "Other gods" are strangers even to those who worship them
11:16.body: Idols are called אלהים אחרים, "other gods". Rashi says they are "other" because they stay strangers to their own worshippers: a person cries out to one and it never answers.

sources.quote: שֶׁהֵם אֲחֵרִים לְעוֹבְדֵיהֶם – צוֹעֵק אֵלָיו וְאֵינוֹ עוֹנֵהוּ
sources.says: Rashi says they are strangers to those who serve them: one cries out to it and it does not answer.

11:18.headline: טוטפת, the head tefillin: "two plus two" in two foreign languages
11:18.body: Onkelos translates טוטפת as tefillin. The Talmud reads the word from two other languages: טט means two in one, פת means two in another. Together they give the four compartments of the head tefillin.

sources.quote: ״טַט״ בְּכַתְפִּי שְׁתַּיִם, ״פַּת״ בְּאַפְרִיקִי שְׁתַּיִם
sources.says: Rabbi Akiva says טט means two in Katfi, and פת means two in Afriki.

sources.quote: וִיהוֹן לִתְפִלִּין בֵּין עֵינֵיכוֹן
sources.says: Onkelos translates "they shall be tefillin between your eyes".

11:21.headline: A land promised "to them", the dead fathers: a hint of resurrection
11:21.body: God swore to the fathers to give the land "to them", not "to you". The fathers had died long before. Rashi says this shows the Torah teaches that the dead will rise.

sources.quote: לָתֵת לָכֶם אֵין כְּתִיב כָּאן, אֶלָּא לָתֵת לָהֶם, מִכָּאן מָצִינוּ לְמֵדִים תְּחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים מִן הַתּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says it does not say "to give to you" but "to give to them", and from here we learn resurrection of the dead from the Torah.

11:22.headline: How can anyone cling to God, a consuming fire?
11:22.body: The verse says to cling to God. Rashi asks how that is possible, since God is a consuming fire. He answers: cling to the wise and their students, and it counts as clinging to God. Ibn Ezra says the clinging comes at the end, and calls it a great secret.

sources.quote: אֶלָּא הִדַּבֵּק בַּתַּלְמִידִים וּבַחֲכָמִים וּמַעֲלֶה אֲנִי עָלֶיךָ כְּאִלּוּ נִדְבַּקְתָּ בּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says to cling to students and sages, and God counts it as if you clung to Him.

sources.quote: ולדבקה בו. בסוף והוא סוד גדול
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the clinging is at the end, and it is a great secret.

11:25.headline: Two kinds of fear: sudden fright and long dread
11:25.body: The verse says "your fright and your dread". Rashi asks if these are the same. He says פחד is a sudden fright, felt by those nearby, and מורא is a long worry, felt by those far away.

sources.quote: פַּחַד לְשׁוֹן בְּעִיתַת פִּתְאֹם, מוֹרָא לְשׁוֹן דְּאָגָה מִיָּמִים רַבִּים
sources.says: Rashi says פחד means sudden terror, and מורא means worry over many days.

12:3.headline: Wipe out their names by giving idols insulting nicknames
12:3.body: The verse says to destroy the idols' names. Rashi says this means renaming them as an insult. Beit Galya becomes Beit Karya, and Ein Kol becomes Ein Kotz, a spring of thorns.

sources.quote: לְכַנּוֹת לָהֶם שֵׁם לִגְנַאי, בֵּית גַּלְיָא — קוֹרִין לָהּ בֵּית כַּרְיָא, עֵין כֹּל — עֵין קוֹץ
sources.says: Rashi says to give them names of shame: Beit Galya is called Beit Karya, and Ein Kol is called Ein Kotz.

12:4.headline: Not doing "so" to God means never erasing his name
12:4.body: Right after the command to smash idols and wipe out their names, the verse says not to do so to God. Rashi and Ramban say the sages learn from this that one may not erase God's name or break a stone off his altar.

sources.quote: אַזְהָרָה לַמּוֹחֵק אֶת הַשֵּׁם וְלַנּוֹתֵץ אֶבֶן מִן הַמִּזְבֵּחַ אוֹ מִן הָעֲזָרָה
sources.says: Rashi says this warns against erasing God's name or pulling a stone from the altar or the Temple court.

sources.quote: וְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל סְמָךְ שֶׁל אַגָּדָה הֵם, אֲבָל הַכָּתוּב כְּדַעַת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ אַזְהָרָה לְמוֹחֵק אֶת הַשֵּׁם
sources.says: Ramban says Rabbi Yishmael's reading is a sermon, but the verse itself, as the sages hold, warns against erasing God's name.

12:23.headline: Why does it take strength not to eat blood?
12:23.body: The verse says "only be strong" not to eat blood. Rashi brings two views. One says the people were used to eating blood. Ben Azzai says blood is easy to avoid, so if even this needs strength, all the more so the other commandments.

sources.quote: מִמַּה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר חֲזַק אַתָּה לָמֵד שֶׁהָיוּ שְׁטוּפִים בַּדָּם לְאָכְלוֹ
sources.says: Rashi brings Rabbi Yehuda: the word "be strong" shows they were steeped in eating blood.

sources.quote: שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עֲזַאי אוֹמֵר לֹא בָא הַכָּתוּב אֶלָּא לְהַזְהִירְךָ וּלְלַמֶּדְךָ עַד כַּמָּה אַתָּה צָרִיךְ לְהִתְחַזֵּק בַּמִּצְווֹת, אִם הַדָּם שֶׁהוּא קַל לְהִשָּׁמֵר מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁאֵין אָדָם מִתְאַוֶּה לוֹ, הֻצְרַךְ לְחַזֶּקְךָ בְאַזְהָרָתוֹ, קַ"וָ לִשְׁאָר מִצְווֹת
sources.says: Rashi brings Ben Azzai: blood is easy to avoid since no one craves it, so if it needs strengthening, the other commandments need it more.

sources.quote: לפי שהדם מובלע בכל האברים, צריך להתחזק ולדקדק יפה להוציאו
sources.says: Rashbam says blood is soaked into all the limbs, so it takes care and effort to remove it.

13:4.headline: "God is testing you": why would God need to find out?
13:4.body: Maimonides says the test is not so that God will know, since he already knows; it is so that the nations will see how firm Israel's faith is. Ramban says a test turns into deeds what was only potential.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 3, Chapter 24
sources.quote: נמצא שאין פירוש דבריו "לדעת הישכם אהבים" (שם יג,ד) הוא "כדי שה' ידע זאת", כי הוא כבר יודע
sources.says: Maimonides says "to know whether you love" does not mean so that God will know, for he already knows.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 3, Chapter 24
sources.quote: שמשמעותם: "כדי שידעו האומות"
sources.says: Maimonides says the meaning is "so that the nations will know".

sources.quote: וְאָמַר לָדַעַת, שֶׁיִּוָּדַע בְּפֹעַל מָה שֶׁהוּא בְּכֹחַ וְגָלוּי לְפָנָיו
sources.says: Ramban says "to know" means to make known in deed what was only potential and already open before God.

sources.quote: כי אין נסיון בשביל הקב״‎ה כי הכל גלוי לפניו
sources.says: Chizkuni says the test is not for God's sake, since everything is open before him.

13:5.headline: How can you cling to God? By copying his kindness
13:5.body: Rashi says clinging to God means following his ways: do kindness, bury the dead and visit the sick, as God himself did. Ibn Ezra reads "walk after God" the same way: act like him as far as you can.

sources.quote: הִדַּבֵּק בִּדְרָכָיו – גְּמֹל חֲסָדִים, קְבֹר מֵתִים, בַּקֵּר חוֹלִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁעָשָׂה הַקָּבָּ"ה
sources.says: Rashi says cling to his ways: do kindness, bury the dead, visit the sick, as God did.

sources.quote: אחרי ה' אלהיכם תלכו. שתעשו על פי יכלתכם כמעשיו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says walking after God means doing, as far as you are able, as he does.

13:6.headline: סרה: words removed from the world, or rebellion?
13:6.body: Rashi says סרה is something removed from the world: it never was, and God never said it. Ibn Ezra prefers the root of סורר, a rebel, and Bekhor Shor reads it as words meant to turn you away from God.

sources.quote: דָּבָר הַמּוּסָר מִן הָעוֹלָם, שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה וְלֹא נִבְרָא וְלֹא צִוִּיתִיו לְדַבֵּר כֵּן
sources.says: Rashi says it is a thing removed from the world, which never was, was not created, and God did not command him to say.

sources.quote: או הוא מגזרת סורר ומורה והוא הנכון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from the root of "stubborn and rebellious", and that this is correct.

sources.quote: דברים כדי להסיר אותך מאחריו
sources.says: Bekhor Shor says it means words meant to turn you away from following God.

13:7.headline: Enticing: advice that sounds right but ends in ruin
13:7.body: Rashi says הסתה means urging someone on. Rashbam says any advice that ends in harm is called הסתה, and HaKtav VeHaKabalah says the enticer presents the act as true and right, not as a gain.

sources.quote: אֵין הֲסָתָה אֶלָּא גֵּרוּי
sources.says: Rashi says enticing means stirring someone up.

sources.quote: יסיתך - כל עצה שסופה פורענות קורא הסתה
sources.says: Rashbam says any advice that ends in disaster is called enticing.

sources.quote: והמסית אומר כי טוב הדבר לעשותו לא להנאה הנמשכת ממנו רק למען האמת והצדק
sources.says: HaKtav VeHaKabalah says the enticer says the act is good to do, not for gain but for the sake of truth and right.

13:9.headline: "Do not consent": do not love him, or do not agree?
13:9.body: Rashi reads לא תאבה as "do not love him", an exception to "love your neighbor as yourself". Ramban says אבה means to be willing, as in "God was not willing to listen to Balaam", so it means do not agree to him.

sources.quote: לֹא תְהֵא תָאֵב לוֹ, לֹא תֶּאֱהָבֶנּוּ
sources.says: Rashi says do not desire him and do not love him.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ויקרא י"ט) וְאָהַבְתָּ לְרֵעֲךָ כָּמוֹךָ
sources.says: Rashi says this is because the Torah says "love your neighbor as yourself".

sources.quote: כִּי אָבָה לְשׁוֹן רָצוֹן, וְלֹא אָבָה ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ לִשְׁמֹעַ אֶל בִּלְעָם
sources.says: Ramban says אבה means being willing, as in "the Lord your God was not willing to listen to Balaam".

13:14.headline: Bnei bliya'al: people "without a yoke"
13:14.body: Rashi splits בליעל into בלי עול, "without a yoke": people who threw off God's yoke. Rabbeinu Bahya also reads it as "one who will not rise" to God's presence.

sources.quote: בני בליעל. בְּלִי עֹל, שֶׁפָּרְקוּ עֻלּוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says בליעל means without a yoke: they threw off God's yoke.

sources.quote: לשון בליעל שלא יעלה במחיצתו של הקב"ה, או בלי עול
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says בליעל means one who will not rise into God's presence, or one without a yoke.

14:1.headline: Do not cut yourselves, and do not split into factions
14:1.body: The plain sense is a ban on gashing your skin in mourning. The Sifrei also hears אגודה, a group, in the word: do not break into separate factions, but be one band.

sources.quote: לֹא תִתְּנוּ גְדִידָה וְשֶׂרֶט בִּבְשַׂרְכֶם עַל מֵת כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁהָאֱמוֹרִיִּים עוֹשִׂין
sources.says: Rashi says it means not to make cuts and gashes in your flesh for the dead, as the Amorites did.

sources.quote: לֹא תִתְגֹּדְדוּ – לֹא תֵעָשׂוּ אֲגֻדּוֹת, אֶלָּא הֱיוּ כֻּלְּכֶם אֲגֻדָּה אַחַת
sources.says: The Sifrei says it means do not form separate groups, but all of you be one group.

sources.quote: אִיקְּרִי כָּאן ״לֹא תִתְגּוֹדְדוּ״, לֹא תֵּעָשׂוּ אֲגוּדּוֹת אֲגוּדּוֹת
sources.says: Resh Lakish asks Rabbi Yohanan whether the verse forbids forming separate factions.

14:13.headline: The bird called ראה is named for how far it sees
14:13.body: The Talmud says this bird is called ראה, the seer, because it sees so far. It can stand in Babylon and spot a carcass in the Land of Israel.

sources.quote: וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמָהּ רָאָה? שֶׁרוֹאָה בְּיוֹתֵר
sources.says: Rashi says it is called ראה because it sees very well.

sources.quote: וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמָהּ רָאָה? שֶׁרוֹאָה בְּיוֹתֵר
sources.says: Rabbi Abahu says it is called ראה because it sees exceptionally far.

sources.quote: עוֹמֶדֶת בְּבָבֶל וְרוֹאָה נְבֵלָה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: A teaching adds that it stands in Babylon and sees a carcass in the Land of Israel.

14:17.headline: When the רחם bird comes, mercy comes
14:17.body: Rabbi Yohanan reads the bird's name from רחמים, mercy: when it comes, mercy comes to the world. Another sage says that if it sits on the ground and whistles, the Messiah is coming.

sources.quote: לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ רָחָם? כֵּיוָן שֶׁבָּא רָחָם בָּאוּ רַחֲמִים לְעוֹלָם
sources.says: Rabbi Yohanan says it is called רחם because when it comes, mercy comes to the world.

sources.quote: וּגְמִירִי דְּאִי יָתֵיב אַאַרְעָא וְשָׁרֵיק – אֲתָא מְשִׁיחָא
sources.says: Rav Bivi says there is a tradition that if it sits on the ground and whistles, the Messiah comes.

14:17.headline: The bird that draws fish out of the sea
14:17.body: The sages read שלך as the bird that draws (שולה) fish out of the sea. When Rabbi Yohanan saw one, he quoted the verse that God's judgments are like the great deep.

sources.quote: הַשּׁוֹלֶה דָּגִים מִן הַיָּם
sources.says: Rashi says it is the bird that draws fish out of the sea.

sources.quote: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, כִּי הֲוָה חָזֵי שָׁלָךְ, אָמַר: ״מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ תְּהוֹם רַבָּה
sources.says: The Talmud says that when Rabbi Yohanan saw a שלך he said, your judgments are a great deep.

14:18.headline: The kind bird, still on the list of forbidden birds
14:18.body: The sages say the stork is called חסידה, the kind one, because it shares its food with its companions. It is still one of the birds the Torah forbids.

sources.quote: לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמָהּ חֲסִידָה? שֶׁעוֹשָׂה חֲסִידוּת עִם חַבְרוֹתֶיהָ
sources.says: Rav Yehudah says it is called חסידה because it does kindness with its companions.

sources.quote: וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמָהּ חֲסִידָה? שֶׁעוֹשָֹׁה חֲסִידוּת עִם חַבְרוֹתֶיהָ בִּמְזוֹנוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says it is called חסידה because it does kindness with its companions in sharing food.

14:18.headline: The bird with a doubled crest, which fetched the shamir
14:18.body: The Talmud reads דוכיפת as הודו כפות, its glory is folded, meaning its crest is doubled. It adds that this is the bird that brought the shamir for building the Temple.

sources.quote: דּוּכִיפַת, שֶׁהוֹדוֹ כָּפוּת, וְזֶהוּ שֶׁהֵבִיא שָׁמִיר לְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
sources.says: The Talmud says it is called דוכיפת because its glory is folded, and that it brought the shamir to the Temple.

sources.quote: וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ דּוּכִיפַת? שֶׁ"הוֹדוֹ כָפוּת" וְזוֹ הִיא כַּרְבָּלְתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is called דוכיפת because its glory is doubled, and its glory is its crest.

14:22.headline: Give a tenth so that you grow rich
14:22.body: עשר, a tenth, sounds like עושר, wealth. The Talmud reads the doubled verb as: give a tenth so that you become rich. Rabbeinu Bahya notes that the verse's words do not literally say wealth.

sources.quote: עַשֵּׂר תְּעַשֵּׂר״ — עַשֵּׂר בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתִּתְעַשֵּׁר
sources.says: The Talmud says: tithe so that you will become rich.

sources.quote: כִּי בְּעִשּׂוּר הַתְּבוּאָה וְהַבְּהֵמָה תִּרְבֶּה הַתְּבוּאָה וְיִרְבֶּה הַמִּקְנֶה
sources.says: Sforno says that by tithing grain and animals, the grain and the herds will grow.

sources.quote: והנה אין בלשון הכתוב לשון עושר
sources.says: Bahya says the wording of the verse has no word for wealth in it.

14:23.headline: Learn to fear God, or get used to it
14:23.body: Ibn Ezra gives two readings. In Jerusalem people will teach you, or the word means training, like a trained calf, so eating there makes fear of God a habit. He prefers the second.

sources.quote: הטעם כי כאשר תלך אל מקום הכבוד שם ילמדוך וטעם שנית להיות למען תלמד כטעם עגלה מלומדה והטעם רגילות והוא הישר בעיני
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means they will teach you there, or else it means habit, like a trained calf, and he thinks the second is right.

sources.quote: תהיה רגיל כמו עגלה מלומדה
sources.says: Chizkuni says it means you will become used to it, like a trained calf.

15:1.headline: Shemittah: the year you let debts drop
15:1.body: Ibn Ezra says the name of the seventh year means letting something drop, as when Jezebel's servants were told 'drop her' (שמטוה) and she fell. In this year a lender lets go of what he is owed.

sources.quote: והטעם כמו שמטוה והניחו' ותפול
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the meaning is like 'drop her', letting something go so that it falls.

15:2.headline: 'For He called a release' means the time has come
15:2.body: קרא usually means 'called'. Rashbam says here it means the time for release has arrived, as when a festival is 'called' at its set time.

sources.quote: כלומר: כי הגיע זמן שמטה כמו: מקראי קדש קרא עלי מועד, קראו צום, כלם לשון זמן
sources.says: Rashbam says it means the time of release has come, as in 'holy convocations' and 'proclaim a fast', all words for a set time.

15:6.headline: One letter decides who is the lender and who the borrower
15:6.body: Rashi says this form of the verb makes you the lender; a plainer form would make you the borrower. Ibn Ezra and Rashbam tie it to עבוט, a pledge: you will hold the nations' pledges.

sources.quote: כָּל לְשׁוֹן הַלְוָאָה כְּשֶׁנּוֹפֵל עַל הַמַּלְוֶה נוֹפֵל בִּלְשׁוֹן מַפְעִיל, כְּגוֹן וְהִלְוִיתָ, וְהַעֲבַטְתָּ. וְאִם הָיָה אוֹמֵר וְעָבַטְתָּ הָיָה נוֹפֵל עַל הַלֹּוֶה
sources.says: Rashi says a word for lending in the causative form refers to the lender, and the simple form would refer to the borrower.

sources.quote: והטעם תקחו עבוטו שהוא משכון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means you will take his pledge, a security.

sources.quote: תקח משכנותם בעל כרחם
sources.says: Rashbam says you will take their pledges against their will for your loans.

15:7.headline: A hand that opens to give and then snaps shut
15:7.body: Ibn Ezra says תקפץ means to close, as a mouth 'shuts'. Rashi reads the two warnings in this verse as two kinds of people: one who agonizes over whether to give, and one who reaches out his hand and then closes it.

sources.quote: תקפוץ. תסגור וכן קפצה פיה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says תקפוץ means to close, as in 'she shut her mouth'.

sources.quote: יֵשׁ לְךָ אָדָם שֶׁמִּצְטַעֵר אִם יִתֵּן אִם לֹא יִתֵּן, לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר "לֹא תְאַמֵּץ". יֵשׁ לְךָ שֶׁפּוֹשֵׁט אֶת יָדוֹ וְקוֹפְצָהּ, לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר "לֹא תִקְפֹּץ"
sources.says: Rashi says one person is torn over whether to give, so it says 'do not harden'; another stretches out his hand and closes it, so it says 'do not shut'.

15:14.headline: Send him off with a gift worn like a necklace
15:14.body: ענק is a necklace. Rashi says the gift should be like jewelry worn high, so all can see you treated him well; others say it means loading the gift onto his neck. Ibn Ezra links it to 'a necklace for your throat' in Proverbs.

sources.quote: העניק תעניק. לְשׁוֹן עֲדִי בַּגֹּבַהּ וּבְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן, דָּבָר שֶׁיְּהֵא נִכָּר שֶׁהֱטִיבוֹתָ לוֹ; וְיֵשׁ מְפָרְשִׁים לְשׁוֹן הַטְעָנָה עַל צַוָּארוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means an ornament worn high and in plain view, something showing you did him good; some explain it as loading onto his neck.

sources.quote: הטעם עשה לו תפארת מגזרת וענקים לגרגרותיך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means giving him honor, from 'necklaces for your throat'.

15:17.headline: A servant 'forever' goes free at the Jubilee
15:17.body: עולם usually means forever. Rashi says here it means until the Jubilee, since in that year every man returns to his family. Fifty years, he says, can be called עולם.

sources.quote: עבד עולם. יָכוֹל כְּמַשְׁמָעוֹ, תַּ"לֹ "וְשַׁבְתֶּם אִישׁ אֶל אֲחֻזָּתוֹ וְאִישׁ אֶל מִשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ תָּשֻׁבוּ" (ויקרא כ"ה), הָא לָמַדְתָּ שֶׁאֵין זֶה אֶלָּא עוֹלָמוֹ שֶׁל יוֹבֵל
sources.says: Rashi says 'forever' cannot mean its plain sense, since at the Jubilee every man returns home; it means the 'world' of the Jubilee.

sources.quote: מַגִּיד שֶׁחֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה קְרוּיִים עוֹלָם
sources.says: Rashi says this shows that fifty years are called עולם.

16:1.headline: The month named for ripening barley
16:1.body: Chizkuni says Nisan is called 'the month of the אביב' because barley, called אביב, ripens in it. Rashi reads 'keep the month' as a duty to watch the calendar so this month falls when the barley is ripe.

sources.quote: חדש ניסן נקרא חדש האביב על שם שהתבואות שנקראו אביב מתבשלות בו והם שעורים
sources.says: Chizkuni says Nisan is called the month of the אביב because the grain called אביב, barley, ripens in it.

sources.quote: מִקֹּדֶם בּוֹאוֹ שְׁמֹר שֶׁיְּהֵא רָאוּי לְאָבִיב
sources.says: Rashi says that before the month comes, you must make sure it will be fit for ripe barley, and if not, add a month to the year.

16:1.headline: They left Egypt by day, so why 'at night'?
16:1.body: Another verse says Israel left Egypt the morning after the Passover. Rashi says 'at night' is when Pharaoh gave them leave to go.

sources.quote: אֶלָּא לְפִי שֶׁבַּלַּיְלָה נָתַן לָהֶם פַּרְעֹה רְשׁוּת לָצֵאת
sources.says: Rashi says they went out by day, but it was at night that Pharaoh gave them permission to leave.

16:3.headline: Whose haste was it, Israel's or Egypt's?
16:3.body: The verse says 'you left in haste', so the dough had no time to rise. Rashi says the haste was really Egypt's, who pressed the people to go.

sources.quote: וְחִפָּזוֹן לֹא שֶׁלְּךָ הָיָה אֶלָּא שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם
sources.says: Rashi says the haste was not Israel's but Egypt's.

16:7.headline: 'Cook it' here means roast it
16:7.body: בשל usually means to boil, yet the Passover lamb is roasted. Rashi says roasting is also called בשול, and Chizkuni says the word means making food ready, as grapes 'ripen' (הבשילו).

sources.quote: זֶהוּ צְלִי אֵשׁ, שֶׁאַף הוּא קָרוּי בִּשּׁוּל
sources.says: Rashi says this means roasting in fire, which is also called cooking.

sources.quote: ובשלת לשון הכנת אוכל והזמנה כמו הבשילו אשכלותיה ענבים
sources.says: Chizkuni says the word means preparing food, like grape clusters that ripen.

16:8.headline: Atzeret: holding back from work, or gathering to feast
16:8.body: Rashi gives two readings of עצרת. Either 'hold yourself back' from work, or a gathering to eat and drink, from the same root as 'let us keep you' for a meal.

sources.quote: עֲצֹר עַצְמְךָ מִן הַמְּלָאכָה; דָּ"אַ — כְּנוּפְיָא שֶׁל מַאֲכָל וּמִשְׁתֶּה
sources.says: Rashi says it means hold yourself back from work, or else a gathering for food and drink.

16:15.headline: 'You shall be only joyful': an order or a promise?
16:15.body: Rashi says that by the plain sense this is not a command but a promise that you will be happy. Ibn Ezra brings both readings: a duty to rejoice on Sukkot, or a promise of lasting joy.

sources.quote: לְפִי פְשׁוּטוֹ אֵין זֶה לְשׁוֹן צִוּוּי אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן הַבְטָחָה
sources.says: Rashi says by the plain sense this is not a command but a promise.

sources.quote: מצוה לשמוח בחג הסוכות וי״א כי יברכך לעתיד ותהיה לעולם שמח
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is a command to rejoice on Sukkot, and reports others who read it as a promise of joy forever.

16:19.headline: 'Words of the righteous' means words that are right
16:19.body: צדיקים usually means righteous people. Rashi reads 'words of the righteous' as words that are just, true rulings, and Chizkuni says the צדיקים are the parties in a case.

sources.quote: דְּבָרִים הַמְצֻדָּקִים – מִשְׁפְּטֵי אֱמֶת
sources.says: Rashi says it means words that are just, true judgments.

sources.quote: דברי צדיקם הם בעלי הדין דוגמא והצדיקו את הצדיק
sources.says: Chizkuni says the צדיקים here are the parties to the case, as in 'they shall declare the righteous one right'.

16:20.headline: Why the verse says 'justice, justice' twice
16:20.body: Ibn Ezra gives reasons for the doubled word: be just whether you gain or lose, be just again and again, or simply for force. The Talmud says one 'justice' is for a ruling and one for a fair compromise.

sources.quote: וטעם שני פעמים לדבר צדק שירויח בו או יפסיד או פעם אחר פעם כל ימי היותך או לחזוק
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word is doubled to mean justice whether you gain or lose, time after time all your life, or for emphasis.

sources.quote: אֶחָד לְדִין וְאֶחָד לִפְשָׁרָה
sources.says: The Talmud says one 'justice' is for strict law and one is for compromise.

16:22.headline: A stone pillar God once loved and now hates
16:22.body: A single stone pillar for offerings was once a way to serve God. Rashi says God loved it in the days of the patriarchs but now hates it, because the Canaanites made it a rite of idol worship.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיְתָה אֲהוּבָה לוֹ בִּימֵי הָאָבוֹת, עַכְשָׁיו שְׂנֵאָהּ מֵאַחַר שֶׁעֲשָׂאוּהָ אֵלּוּ חֹק לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
sources.says: Rashi says the pillar was beloved to God in the days of the patriarchs, but now He hates it since the Canaanites made it a rite of idol worship.

17:1.headline: 'Any bad thing': a blemish, or a bad word
17:1.body: דבר can mean a thing or a word. Ibn Ezra reads 'any bad thing' as any blemish on the animal. Rashi, from the Talmud, hears 'a bad word': a warning against spoiling a holy offering by what is said while offering it.

sources.quote: כל דבר רע. פירוש מום
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'any bad thing' means a blemish.

sources.quote: אַזְהָרָה לַמְפַגֵּל בַּקֳּדָשִׁים עַ"יְ דִּבּוּר רָע
sources.says: Rashi says it is a warning against invalidating holy offerings through bad speech.

17:3.headline: Why say God 'did not command' sun worship?
17:3.body: Of course God never commanded idol worship, so why say it? Rabbeinu Bahya says people who served the sun and moon thought that honoring the king's servants honors the king. The verse says God never asked for that. Rashi fills in the short phrase: which I did not command you to worship.

sources.quote: דבר ידוע כי הקב"ה לא צוה לעבוד עבודה זרה, א"כ מה טעם לומר אשר לא צויתי
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya asks why the verse says 'which I did not command', since it is obvious God never commanded idol worship.

sources.quote: חושבים כי בעבודתם ימצאו חן בעיני ה' יתעלה בעבור שהם משרתי המלך
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says they thought serving these powers would win God's favor, since they are the King's servants.

sources.quote: אשר לא צויתי. לְעָבְדָם
sources.says: Rashi says it means: which I did not command you to worship.

17:5.headline: Which gate: the court's, or where the idol was served?
17:5.body: Chizkuni reads 'your gates' plainly as the place of judgment, since courts sat at the city gate. Rashi says that reading is a mistake: the sages compare this verse to verse 2, so it is the gate where he worshipped. Sforno says this shows the idol could not save him there.

sources.quote: אל שעריך לפי הפשט הוא מקום המשפט
sources.says: Chizkuni says that by the plain sense 'your gates' is the place of judgment.

sources.quote: אַף שְׁעָרֶיךָ הָאָמוּר לְמַטָּה שַׁעַר שֶׁעָבַד בּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says 'your gates' here, like 'your gates' above, is the gate where he worshipped.

sources.quote: אֶל שַׁעַר שֶׁעָבַד בּוֹ, לְהַרְאוֹת שֶׁלֹּא יוֹשִׁיעֵהוּ הָאֱלִיל הַנֶּעֱבָד שָׁם
sources.says: Sforno says it is the gate where he worshipped, to show that the idol served there will not save him.

17:6.headline: 'The dead man shall be put to death'?
17:6.body: The phrase sounds odd: how can a dead man be put to death? Chizkuni says המת means the one who is going to die, as Jacob says 'I am dying'. Shadal compares other doubled phrases, like 'if the one who falls should fall', meaning whoever it may be.

sources.quote: יומת המת העתיד להיות מת
sources.says: Chizkuni says 'the dead man' means the one who is going to die.

sources.quote: יומת המת: כמו כי יפול הנופל
sources.says: Shadal says it is like 'if the one who falls should fall'.

17:6.headline: Two witnesses suffice, so why mention three?
17:6.body: Rashi says three witnesses count as one testimony, just like two. Ramban, cited by Rabbeinu Bahya, says that if more people saw it, the court should bring them all, since more witnesses make the truth clearer. A midrash adds that a third false witness is punished like the other two.

sources.quote: אִם מִתְקַיֶּמֶת עֵדוּת בִּשְׁנַיִם לָמָּה פֵּרֵט לְךָ בִשְׁלוֹשָׁה? לְהַקִּישׁ שְׁלוֹשָׁה לִשְׁנַיִם
sources.says: Rashi asks why three is mentioned if two suffice, and answers that it compares three to two.

sources.quote: נשלח בעבורם ויבאו לפנינו, שמתוך רבוי העדים יתברר הענין יותר
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya, citing Ramban, says we send for all the witnesses, since more witnesses make the matter clearer.

sources.quote: ולמדך הכתוב שכל הנטפל לעוברי עברה נענש כעוברי עברה
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya cites a midrash: whoever joins wrongdoers is punished like them.

17:8.headline: Not a 'wonder' here, but a case hidden from you
17:8.body: פלא usually means a wonder. Rashi says here it means set apart: a case too hidden for the local judges to see through. Rabbeinu Bahya compares God's question to Abraham about Sarah: 'Is anything too hidden for the Lord?'

sources.quote: כָּל הַפְלָאָה לְשׁוֹן הַבְדָּלָה וּפְרִישָׁה, שֶׁהַדָּבָר נִבְדָּל וּמְכֻסֶּה מִמְּךָ
sources.says: Rashi says every use of הפלאה means separation: the matter is set apart and hidden from you.

sources.quote: כי יפלא ממך דבר. לשון העלמה, כמו (בראשית י״ח:י״ד) היפלא מה' דבר
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says it means hiddenness, as in 'Is anything hidden from the Lord?'

17:8.headline: Whose quarrel: the judges', or the two sides'?
17:8.body: Rashi says 'matters of dispute' means the wise men of the city disagree, one saying pure and one impure. Shadal objects that a disagreement among scholars is not a ריב, a quarrel. He says it means the two parties argue so hard that the judges cannot decide.

sources.quote: שֶׁיִּהְיוּ חַכְמֵי הָעִיר חוֹלְקִים בַּדָּבָר, זֶה מְטַמֵּא וְזֶה מְטַהֵר
sources.says: Rashi says it means the city's sages disagree, one declaring impure and one pure.

sources.quote: כי מחלוקת החכמים איננה ריב
sources.says: Shadal says a disagreement among sages is not called a quarrel.

sources.quote: שבעלי הריב מתעצמים בטענותיהם
sources.says: Shadal says it means the parties to the case press their claims hard against each other.

17:9.headline: The judge 'in those days': the one you have
17:9.body: Why add 'who will be in those days'? Rashi says: even if he is not like the judges before him, you must listen to him. You only have the judge of your own time. Rabbeinu Bahya puts it this way: Jephthah in his generation is like Samuel in his.

sources.quote: וַאֲפִלּוּ אֵינוֹ כִּשְׁאָר שׁוֹפְטִים שֶׁהָיוּ לְפָנָיו, אַתָּה צָרִיךְ לִשְׁמֹעַ לוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says that even if he is not like the judges before him, you must listen to him.

sources.quote: אין לך אלא שופט שבימיך, יפתח בדורו כשמואל בדורו
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says you have only the judge of your days: Jephthah in his generation is like Samuel in his.

17:11.headline: Even if they call right left
17:11.body: Rashi says 'do not turn right or left' means: follow the high court even if it tells you right is left. Ramban adds: even if you are sure they are wrong. Otherwise opinions would split and the Torah would become many Torahs.

sources.quote: אֲפִלּוּ אוֹמֵר לְךָ עַל יָמִין שֶׁהוּא שְׂמֹאל וְעַל שְׂמֹאל שֶׁהוּא יָמִין
sources.says: Rashi says you must obey even if they tell you right is left and left is right.

sources.quote: וְעִנְיָנוֹ אֲפִלּוּ תַּחְשֹׁב בְּלִבְּךָ שֶׁהֵם טוֹעִים
sources.says: Ramban says it means even if you think in your heart that they are mistaken.

sources.quote: והדעות לא ישתוו בכל הדברים הנולדים ואז ירבו המחלוקות ותעשה התורה כמה תורות
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya, citing Ramban, says opinions will differ on new questions, disputes will multiply, and the Torah would become many Torahs.

17:15.headline: Appoint a king: allowed, or required?
17:15.body: Ibn Ezra reads 'you shall surely set a king' as permission. Rabbeinu Bahya and Bekhor Shor read it as a command. Bekhor Shor says there must be a king, so that each person does not do what is right in his own eyes.

sources.quote: שום תשים. רשות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'you shall set' is a permission.

sources.quote: ע"ד הפשט זו מצות עשה שיהיה בישראל מלך
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says that by the plain sense it is a command that Israel have a king.

sources.quote: כי ודאי צריך שיהא מלך, שלא יעשה כל אחד את הישר בעיניו
sources.says: Bekhor Shor says there certainly must be a king, so that each person does not do what is right in his own eyes.

17:16.headline: 'You shall not return that way': where did God say it?
17:16.body: No earlier verse says this in so many words. Ibn Ezra says it was a command given but not written down. Ramban brings the sages' reading: it is Moses' word at the sea, 'the Egyptians you see today you will never see again', taken as a command.

sources.quote: לא תוסיפון. מצוה היתה ולא נכתבה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it was a commandment that was not written down.

sources.quote: כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר רְאִיתֶם אֶת מִצְרַיִם הַיּוֹם לֹא תֹסִיפוּ לִרְאֹתָם עוֹד עַד עוֹלָם
sources.says: Ramban says that by the sages' view it is the verse 'as you have seen Egypt today, you shall never see them again'.

17:20.headline: Even a small command from a prophet
17:20.body: Rashi says 'not turning from the commandment' covers even a light command given by a prophet. Saul lost his kingdom because he did not wait for Samuel the full seven days, as he had been told.

sources.quote: ולבלתי סור מן המצוה. אֲפִלּוּ מִצְוָה קַלָּה שֶׁל נָבִיא
sources.says: Rashi says it means not turning from even a light command of a prophet.

sources.quote: וְכֵן מָצִינוּ בְשָׁאוּל שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ שְׁמוּאֵל (שמואל א י') "שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תּוֹחֵל עַד בּוֹאִי אֵלֶיךָ"
sources.says: Rashi points to Saul, whom Samuel told to wait seven days until he came.

18:3.headline: Arm, cheeks, stomach: the priest's gifts recall Pinchas
18:3.body: Rashi cites interpreters who tie each gift to Pinchas: the arm for the spear in his hand, the cheeks for his prayer, and the stomach for where his spear struck the woman. Ibn Ezra says that in the plain sense these are simply the best cuts.

sources.quote: דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת הָיוּ אוֹמְרִים זְרוֹעַ תַּחַת יַד
sources.says: Rashi says interpreters taught that the arm is in return for the hand of Pinchas that took the spear.

sources.quote: לְחָיַיִם תַּחַת תְּפִלָּה
sources.says: Rashi says the cheeks are in return for his prayer.

sources.quote: וְהַקֵּבָה תַּחַת "הָאִשָּׁה אֶל קֳבָתָהּ"
sources.says: Rashi says the stomach is in return for piercing the woman through her belly.

sources.quote: ועל דרך הפשט כי אלה טובים משאר הבשר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says in the plain sense these parts are better than the rest of the meat.

18:9.headline: Do not learn to do it, but you may learn to understand
18:9.body: Rashi says the verse forbids learning these practices to do them, but you may study them to see how corrupt they are and to teach your children. Bahya adds that the high court had to know even sorcery in order to judge.

sources.quote: אֲבָל אַתָּה לָמֵד לְהָבִין וּלְהוֹרוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says you may learn in order to understand and to teach.

sources.quote: לְהָבִין מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם כַּמָּה הֵם מְקֻלְקָלִים
sources.says: Rashi says to understand how corrupt their practices are.

sources.quote: וכן מצינו בשבעים סנהדרין שהיו צריכין להיותם בקיאים בכל החכמות אפילו בחכמת הכשפים
sources.says: Bahya says the seventy judges of the Sanhedrin had to be expert in every field, even in sorcery.

18:10.headline: מעונן: one who reads lucky times, fools eyes, or watches clouds
18:10.body: Rabbi Akiva reads מעונן from עונה, a time: one who says a certain hour is lucky for starting. The sages read it from עין, eye, one who fools the eyes, and Bahya adds a third sense, from ענן, one who reads the clouds.

sources.quote: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר אֵלּוּ נוֹתְנֵי עוֹנוֹת – שֶׁאוֹמְרִים עוֹנָה פְּלוֹנִית יָפָה לְהַתְחִיל
sources.says: Rashi cites Rabbi Akiva: these are people who fix times, saying a certain time is good to begin.

sources.quote: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים אֵלּוּ אוֹחֲזֵי הָעֵינַיִם
sources.says: Rashi cites the sages: these are people who trick the eyes.

sources.quote: מעונן, יש בו שלש משמעיות, לשון עונה, לשון עין, לשון ענן
sources.says: Bahya says מעונן has three senses: from time, from eye, and from cloud.

18:11.headline: A joiner of joinings: the charmer who gathers snakes
18:11.body: חבר means to join. Rashi says this charmer gathers snakes, scorpions or other creatures into one place, Ibn Ezra says it means those who claim to join demons together, and Onkelos translates it as one who mutters spells.

sources.quote: שֶׁמְּצָרֵף נְחָשִׁים אוֹ עַקְרַבִּים אוֹ שְׁאָר חַיּוֹת לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד
sources.says: Rashi says he gathers snakes, scorpions or other creatures into one place.

sources.quote: וחבר חבר. אלה האומרים שיחברו השדים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says these are people who claim to join the demons together.

sources.quote: וְרָטִין רְטָן
sources.says: Onkelos translates it as one who mutters charms.

18:12.headline: בגלל, because of, heard as a turning wheel
18:12.body: Bahya hears גלגל, a wheel, in בגלל: God turns the wheel of the heavens and overrules the stars to drive these nations out. He cites a similar teaching of the sages about charity: it is a wheel that turns in the world.

sources.quote: מהפך הגלגל ומשדד המזלות להורישם מפניך, וזהו לשון בגלל
sources.says: Bahya says God turns the wheel and overrules the stars to drive them out before you, and this is the meaning of בגלל.

sources.quote: כי בגלל הדבר הזה, גלגל הוא שחוזר בעולם
sources.says: Bahya cites the sages on the verse about charity: because of this thing, it is a wheel that turns in the world.

19:5.headline: Did the axe head fly off, or a chip of wood?
19:5.body: ונשל הברזל מן העץ can mean the iron slipped off its wooden handle. Or it can mean the iron knocked a chip off the tree being chopped, and the chip killed. Rashi brings both views from the sages, and Rashbam takes the second.

sources.quote: יֵשׁ מֵרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אוֹמְרִים נִשְׁמַט הַבַּרְזֶל מִקַּתּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says some of the sages read it as the iron slipping off its handle.

sources.quote: שֶׁיִּשַּׁל הַבַּרְזֶל חֲתִיכָה מִן הָעֵץ הַמִּתְבַּקֵּעַ וְהִיא נִתְּזָה וְהָרְגָה
sources.says: Rashi says others read it as the iron knocking a piece off the wood being split, which flew and killed.

sources.quote: שישליך הגרזן חתיכת בקעת מן העץ שהוא מבקע
sources.says: Rashbam says the axe throws off a chip from the wood it is splitting.

19:8.headline: 'If' God widens your border, or 'when' He does?
19:8.body: The Sifrei reads ואם as a condition: keep this command, and as a reward God will widen your land. Rabbeinu Bahya reads it as a sure promise, since the verse says God swore it.

sources.quote: עֲשֵׂה מִצְוָה הָאֲמוּרָה בָּעִנְיָן, שֶׁבִּשְׂכָרָהּ יַרְחִיב
sources.says: The Sifrei says to do the command in this passage, and as its reward God will widen your border.

sources.quote: ולשון ואם לשון ודאי, ויורה על זה מה שאמר כאשר נשבע
sources.says: Bahya says ואם here means 'surely', as shown by the words 'as He swore'.

sources.quote: לָתֵת לְךָ אֶרֶץ קֵינִי וּקְנִזִּי וְקַדְמוֹנִי
sources.says: Rashi says the wider border is the land of the Kenite, Kenizzite and Kadmonite promised to Abraham.

19:16.headline: סרה: a sin, or a witness 'removed' from his own story
19:16.body: The Sifrei says סרה simply means a transgression. Rashi hears the root סור, to remove: the witness is shown he could not have been there, because others say 'you were with us that day'.

sources.quote: אֵין סָרָה אֶלָּא עֲבֵרָה
sources.says: The Sifrei says סרה means nothing but a transgression.

sources.quote: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ, שֶׁהוּסַר הָעֵד הַזֶּה מִכָּל הָעֵדוּת הַזֹּאת
sources.says: Rashi says it is something untrue, where this witness is removed from the whole testimony.

sources.quote: וַהֲלֹא עִמָּנוּ הֱיִיתֶם אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם בְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי
sources.says: Rashi says this happens when others tell them: you were with us that day in another place.

19:17.headline: Standing before the judges is standing before God
19:17.body: The verse says the two sides stand 'before the LORD', then 'before the priests and the judges'. Rashi says they should feel as if they stand before God. Bahya says the judge is called here by God's own name.

sources.quote: יִהְיֶה דּוֹמֶה לָהֶם כְּאִלּוּ עוֹמְדִין לִפְנֵי הַמָּקוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says it should seem to them as if they are standing before God.

sources.quote: לבאר שהשופט נקרא בשם המיוחד
sources.says: Bahya says the verse shows that the judge is called by God's unique name.

19:18.headline: One 'witness' in the Torah usually means two
19:18.body: The verse says 'the witness is a false witness', in the singular. Rashi and Bahya say that wherever the Torah says עד, a witness, it means a pair, unless it says 'one witness'.

sources.quote: כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר עֵד — בִּשְׁנַיִם הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר
sources.says: Rashi says every place that says 'witness', the verse is speaking of two.

sources.quote: כל מקום שנאמר בתורה עד הם שנים עד שיפרוט הכתוב עד אחד
sources.says: Bahya says every 'witness' in the Torah means two, until the verse spells out 'one witness'.

2:3.headline: Turn north, or hide yourselves: צפון also means hidden
2:3.body: צפנה means northward, but the same letters mean to hide. The midrash reads it as advice: hide yourselves from Esau until his time passes, or hide yourselves in the Torah.

sources.quote: אִם רְאִיתֶם אוֹתוֹ שֶׁמְבַקֵּשׁ לְהִתְגָּרוֹת בָּכֶם אַל תַּעַמְדוּ כְּנֶגְדוֹ אֶלָּא הַצְפִּינוּ עַצְמְכֶם מִמֶּנּוּ עַד שֶׁיַּעֲבֹר עוֹלָמוֹ
sources.says: Rabbi Hiyya says that if Esau tries to provoke you, do not stand against him but hide yourselves until his time passes.

sources.quote: וְאֵין צָפֹנָה אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (משלי ב, ז): יִצְפֹּן לַיְשָׁרִים תּוּשִׁיָּה
sources.says: Another rabbi says צפנה means the Torah, because Proverbs says God hides away wisdom for the upright.

2:6.headline: A rare word for buying, still used by the coast
2:6.body: תכרו means you shall buy. Rashi compares Jacob's words אשר כריתי לי, 'which I bought for myself', and notes that in the coastal towns selling was called כירה.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן מֶקַח, וְכֵן "אֲשֶׁר כָּרִיתִי לִי" (בראשית נ'), שֶׁכֵּן בִּכְרַכֵּי הַיָּם קוֹרִין לִמְכִירָה כִּירָה
sources.says: Rashi says the word means buying, like 'which I bought for myself', since in the coastal towns they call selling כירה.

2:7.headline: God 'knew' your journey means God took care of it
2:7.body: ידע usually means knew. Sforno says here it means God provided everything the journey needed. Shadal says it is the knowing of watchful care, as in 'the Lord knows the way of the righteous'.

sources.quote: יָדַע לֶכְתְּךָ. תִּקֵּן אוֹתוֹ בְּכָל הַמֻּצְטָרֵךְ
sources.says: Sforno says 'knew your going' means God arranged everything you needed for it.

sources.quote: ידע לכתך: כמו יודע ה' דרך צדיקים, נכח ה' דרככם, ענין השגחה
sources.says: Shadal says the word means God's watchful care, as in 'the Lord knows the way of the righteous'.

2:9.headline: With Moab only war is banned; with Ammon, any provoking
2:9.body: Rashi notes that for Moab the verse adds מלחמה, war: Israel may not fight them but may still frighten them. For Ammon in verse 19 any provoking is banned. That is a reward for their mother, who did not make her father's act public, as her older sister did by naming her son Moab.

sources.quote: לֹא אָסַר לָהֶם עַל מוֹאָב אֶלָּא מִלְחָמָה, אֲבָל מְיָרְאִים הָיוּ אוֹתָם
sources.says: Rashi says God forbade only war against Moab, but Israel could still frighten them.

sources.quote: בִּשְׂכַר צְנִיעוּת אִמָּם, שֶׁלֹּא פִרְסְמָה עַל אָבִיהָ כְּמוֹ שֶׁעָשְׂתָה הַבְּכִירָה שֶׁקָּרְאָה שֵׁם בְּנָהּ מוֹאָב
sources.says: Rashi says Ammon got the fuller protection because their mother was modest and did not make public what happened with her father, unlike the older sister who named her son Moab.

2:11.headline: Refaim: giants who made people's hands go weak
2:11.body: Rashi hears the verb רפה, to go slack, in the name רפאים. They were called this because anyone who saw them felt his hands go weak.

sources.quote: כָּעֲנָקִים הַנִּקְרָאִים רְפָאִים, עַל שֵׁם שֶׁכָּל הָרוֹאֶה אוֹתָם יָדָיו מִתְרַפּוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says the giants were called Refaim because the hands of anyone who saw them went weak.

2:12.headline: Horites and Hivites: two snake names for one people
2:12.body: The Tur HaArokh says the Horites are the Hivites. חוי suggests a snake on the road, and חורי the snake's hole. Chizkuni says they were called Hivites because they sniffed the land like a snake.

sources.quote: ויתכן שנקרא חוי על שם שהיה נחש עלי דרך ונקרא חורי ע"ש מחור פתן
sources.says: The Tur HaArokh suggests the people was called Hivi after a snake on the road and Hori after the hole of a snake.

sources.quote: עיקר שמם חורי ואינו משבע עממים והא דקרי להו חוי משום דמריחי לארעא כי חיויא
sources.says: Chizkuni says their real name is Horite, and they are called Hivite because they smell out the land like a snake.

2:17.headline: After 38 years God 'speaks' with Moses again
2:17.body: Rashi notes that since the spies, this section says only ויאמר, 'said'. Now it says וידבר, 'spoke'. For the 38 years Israel was in disgrace, God did not speak with Moses with affection. Chizkuni explains that דבור is the long talk of two friends, while אמירה is a few words.

sources.quote: לֹא נֶאֱמַר בְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ וַיְדַבֵּר אֶלָּא וַיֹּאמֶר, לְלַמֶּדְךָ שֶׁכָּל ל"ח שָׁנָה שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל נְזוּפִים, לֹא נִתְיַחֵד עִמּוֹ הַדִּבּוּר בִּלְשׁוֹן חִבָּה
sources.says: Rashi says the section used ויאמר, not וידבר, to teach that for 38 years, while Israel was rebuked, God did not speak with Moses in words of affection.

sources.quote: פירוש דבור משמע מפיו רבוי דברים והוא ענין חיבה כגון שני אוהבים שמדברים זה עם זה מתוך חבה
sources.says: Chizkuni says דבור means many words, a sign of affection, like two friends talking warmly together.

2:20.headline: Zamzummim: the schemers, who could do whatever they planned
2:20.body: Chizkuni says the Ammonites named these giants for their plots and war plans. The Tur HaArokh hears the verb זמם, to plan, doubled: so strong that nothing they planned was beyond them.

sources.quote: והעמונים יקראו להם זמזמים על שם מחשבות ותחבולות מלחמות
sources.says: Chizkuni says they were called Zamzummim for their schemes and plans of war.

sources.quote: מלשון זממו אל תפק אלא שנכפל כלומר עם לא יבצר מהם כל אשר זממו לעשו' מרוב חזקם
sources.says: The Tur HaArokh says the name comes from זמם, to plan, doubled: a people so strong that nothing they planned was out of reach.

2:23.headline: The Avvim: ruiners of their land, or snake-wise people
2:23.body: Rashbam brings the Talmud's reading: they were called Avvim because they ruined (עיוו) their place. He adds a view that they knew the soil like a snake, and in Galilee a snake was called עיויא. The Tur HaArokh says the Avvim are the Hivites, since a snake twists itself.

sources.quote: ולמה נקראו עוים? שעיוו את מקומם
sources.says: Rashbam, citing the Talmud, says they were called Avvim because they ruined their place.

sources.quote: שהיו בקיאין בעפרות כנחש בגלילא צווחין לחיויא עיויא
sources.says: Rashbam cites a view that they knew the soil like a snake, since in Galilee people called a snake עיויא.

sources.quote: ועל דעתי כי העוים הם חוים כי המנהג בלשון שיחליפו השמות בהיותם מורים על ענין אחד והנחש יעוות עצמו
sources.says: The Tur HaArokh holds that the Avvim are the Hivites, because a snake twists (יעוות) itself.

2:24.headline: Begin to inherit, or: I made his land free for you
2:24.body: החל means begin. Rabbeinu Bahya brings the sages' reading from חולין, ordinary or unholy: God made Sihon's land free for Israel to take. The land had passed from Ammon and Moab to Sihon, so it was no longer off limits.

sources.quote: ודרשו רז"ל החל רש, עשיתי ארצו חולין לפניך. והכוונה בזה כי עמון ומואב טיהרו בסיחון
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya cites the sages: 'I made his land חולין before you', meaning Ammon and Moab's land became permitted once Sihon took it.

2:26.headline: From the desert of Kedemot, or from what came first
2:26.body: Kedemot is a place name, and Chizkuni reads it as the eastern desert. Rashi also hears קדם, before: Moses learned to offer peace first from the Torah, which came before the world, or from God, who was before the world.

sources.quote: לָמַדְתִּי מִמִּדְבַּר סִינַי – מִן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁקָּדְמָה לָעוֹלָם
sources.says: Rashi has Moses say he learned it from the Torah, which preceded the world.

sources.quote: מִמְּךָ לָמַדְתִּי, שֶׁקָּדַמְתָּ לָעוֹלָם
sources.says: In a second reading, Moses says to God: I learned it from You, who came before the world.

sources.quote: ממדבר קדמות לשון קדמה מזרחה ממדבר שבמזרח
sources.says: Chizkuni reads קדמות as east: the desert on the east side.

2:28.headline: 'With my feet' means with my troops
2:28.body: Rabbeinu Bahya reads ברגלי, with my feet, as with my hosts, the people who walk behind me. Maimonides lists רגל as a word with several senses, one being those who follow after someone.

sources.quote: רק אעברה ברגלי, בצבאותי
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya explains 'only let me pass with my feet' as with my troops.

sources.quote: יש לו גם משמעות של הליכה בעקבות: "צֵא אַתָּה וְכָל הָעָם אֲשֶׁר בְּרַגְלֶיךָ"
sources.says: Maimonides says רגל has several senses, among them walking after someone, as in 'all the people at your feet'.

2:33.headline: Written 'his son', read 'his sons'
2:33.body: The written text has בנו, his son, though it is read as בניו, his sons. Rashi says the spelling points to one son as mighty as Sihon himself.

sources.quote: בנו כְתִיב, שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ בֵן גִּבּוֹר כְּמוֹתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is written 'his son' because Sihon had a son as mighty as he was.

2:35.headline: Here they plundered eagerly; with Og, they scorned the spoil
2:35.body: Here the word is בזזנו, from plunder. At Og's battle (3:7) it is בזונו, which sounds like contempt. Rashi, from the Sifrei, says Sihon's spoil was precious to them, but by Og's battle they were full and threw much of it away.

sources.quote: בְּבִזַּת סִיחוֹן נֶאֱמַר בָּזַזְנוּ לָנוּ, לְשׁוֹן בִּזָּה, שֶׁהָיְתָה חֲבִיבָה עֲלֵיהֶם וּבוֹזְזִים אִישׁ לוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says Sihon's spoil is called בזזנו, plunder, because it was dear to them and each man grabbed for himself.

sources.quote: לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר בַּזּוֹנוּ לָנוּ, לְשׁוֹן בִּזָּיוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says Og's spoil is called בזונו, from contempt, because by then they were full and scorned it.

20:1.headline: A whole cavalry, and God counts it as one horse
20:1.body: The verse says סוס, horse, in the singular, for a great army. Rashi hears God speaking: in my eyes they are all like one horse, as Gideon was told he would strike Midian 'like one man'.

sources.quote: בְּעֵינַי כֻּלָּם כְּסוּס אֶחָד, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר (שופטים ו') וְהִכִּיתָ אֶת מִדְיָן כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד
sources.says: Rashi says that in God's eyes they are all like one horse, as Judges says 'you will strike Midian like one man'.

20:3.headline: 'Hear, O Israel': the words of the Shema before battle
20:3.body: The priest opens with שמע ישראל, the same words as the daily Shema. Rashi says this is the point: even if you had no merit but saying the Shema, it would be enough for God to save you.

sources.quote: אֲפִלּוּ אֵין בָּכֶם זְכוּת אֶלָּא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע בִּלְבַד, כְּדַאי אַתֶּם שֶׁיּוֹשִׁיעַ אֶתְכֶם
sources.says: Rashi says that even if your only merit is reciting the Shema, you are worthy of being saved.

sources.quote: בזכות שמע ישראל שהוא פרשת היחוד אתם נוצחין
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says you win by the merit of the Shema, the passage of God's oneness.

20:7.headline: 'Lest he die': a warning, and a lesson about dying young
20:7.body: Rashi reads 'go home lest he die' as a warning: if he does not obey the priest and go, he deserves to die. Ibn Ezra draws a different lesson: one who dies in battle dies before his time.

sources.quote: שֶׁאִם לֹא יִשְׁמַע לְדִבְרֵי הַכֹּהֵן כְּדַאי הוּא שֶׁיָּמוּת
sources.says: Rashi says that if he does not listen to the priest, he deserves to die.

sources.quote: רק המת במלחמה מת בלא יומו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says one who dies in war dies before his day.

20:8.headline: Afraid of battle, or afraid of his own sins?
20:8.body: Rabbi Akiva reads 'the fearful man' plainly: he cannot face a drawn sword. Rabbi Yose the Galilean says he fears the sins on his hands. On his view, the excuses for the house, vineyard and bride give cover, so no one knows why a man went home.

sources.quote: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר כְּמַשְׁמָעוֹ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לַעֲמֹד בְּקִשְׁרֵי הַמִּלְחָמָה וְלִרְאוֹת חֶרֶב שְׁלוּפָה
sources.says: Rashi cites Rabbi Akiva: it means what it says, one who cannot stand the battle or see a drawn sword.

sources.quote: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר הַיָּרֵא מֵעֲבֵרוֹת שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ
sources.says: Rashi cites Rabbi Yose the Galilean: it is one who fears the sins he has done.

sources.quote: וְהָרוֹאֵהוּ חוֹזֵר אוֹמֵר שֶׁמָּא בָּנָה בַיִת אוֹ נָטַע כֶּרֶם אוֹ אֵרַשׂ אִשָּׁה
sources.says: Rashi says that whoever sees him go back will think he built a house, planted a vineyard or became engaged.

20:13.headline: 'All its males' means the grown men
20:13.body: The next verse spares 'the children'. Rashi says that includes boys, so זכורה, its males, here means only the adult men.

sources.quote: אַף טַף שֶׁל זְכָרִים, וּמָה אֲנִי מְקַיֵּם "וְהִכִּיתָ אֶת כָל זְכוּרָהּ"? בַּגְּדוֹלִים
sources.says: Rashi says the children spared include boys, so 'all its males' refers to the grown men.

20:17.headline: Six nations named; 'as commanded' brings in the seventh
20:17.body: Only six of the seven nations are listed here. Rashi says 'as the Lord commanded you' adds the missing one, the Girgashites. Rabbeinu Bahya notes they were the smallest of the seven.

sources.quote: כאשר צוך. לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַגִּרְגָּשִׁי
sources.says: Rashi says 'as He commanded you' comes to include the Girgashites.

sources.quote: הזכיר בכאן ששה עממין ולא הזכיר השביעי שהוא הגרגשי, לפי שהיה מעט וקטן שבכלן
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says six nations are named and the seventh, the Girgashites, is left out because it was the smallest.

20:20.headline: Until it falls, or until it bows to you
20:20.body: Rashbam reads רדתה from ירד, to go down: until its walls come down. Rashi reads it from רדה, to rule: until the city is bent under you.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן רִדּוּי, שֶׁתְּהֵא כְּפוּפָה לְךָ
sources.says: Rashi says the word means subjugation, until the city is bent under you.

sources.quote: עד רדת חומותיה. כדכתיב: עד רדת חומותיך הגבוהות והבצורות
sources.says: Rashbam says it means until its walls come down, as another verse says 'until your high, fortified walls come down'.

21:11.headline: The sages read 'woman of' as including a married captive
21:11.body: The verse uses the joined form אשת, 'woman of', where אשה would do. Rashi and Rabbeinu Bahya say the sages read this as including even a woman who is already married.

sources.quote: אֲפִלּוּ אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ
sources.says: Rashi says the word includes even a married woman.

sources.quote: הזכיר אשת בסמיכות, ודרשו רז"ל אפילו אשת איש
sources.says: Bahya notes the verse uses the joined form אשת, and the sages read it as 'even a married woman'.

21:12.headline: 'She shall do her nails': let them grow, or cut them?
21:12.body: The verse only says she shall 'do' her nails. Rashi says she lets them grow so she looks unkempt, while Rabbi Eliezer and Ibn Ezra say she cuts them.

sources.quote: תְּגַדְּלֵם כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּתְנַוֵּל
sources.says: Rashi says she lets her nails grow so that she becomes unattractive.

sources.quote: רְאָיָה לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וְלֹא עָשָׂה רַגְלָיו וְלֹא עָשָׂה שְׂפָמוֹ
sources.says: Ramban cites the Sifrei's proof for Rabbi Eliezer, who reads it as cutting, from a verse where a man 'had not done his feet or his moustache'.

sources.quote: וְכֵן קְצִיצַת הַצִּפָּרְנַיִם אֲבֵלוּת כְּגִלּוּחַ הָרֹאשׁ
sources.says: Ramban says cutting the nails is a sign of mourning, like shaving the head.

sources.quote: ועשתה. תיקון. ותקונה לכרות העודף
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'doing' here means trimming, cutting off the extra.

21:20.headline: 'Glutton and drunkard': the sages read the words from Proverbs
21:20.body: זולל וסבא are rare words. Rashi reads them through Proverbs 23:20, 'drinkers of wine, gluttons of meat', so the rebel son is only guilty for eating meat and drinking wine.

sources.quote: אַל תְּהִי בְּסֹבְאֵי יָיִן בְּזֹלְלֵי בָשָׂר לָמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the son is not liable until he eats a set amount of meat and drinks half a log of wine, learning this from Proverbs.

sources.quote: זָלֵל בְּסָר וְסָבֵי חֲמַר
sources.says: Onkelos translates: a glutton for meat and a guzzler of wine.

sources.quote: זולל. מפורש והוא זולל בשר רק הוא שם כלל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says זולל is a glutton for meat, but is also a general word for someone who gives in to every craving.

22:1.headline: Shutting your eyes to a lost animal, and when it is allowed
22:1.body: Rashi says והתעלמת means shutting your eyes as if you did not see the lost animal. By the plain sense the verse forbids this. The sages read the same word as allowing it at times, for example when the task is beneath an old man's dignity.

sources.quote: כּוֹבֵשׁ עַיִן כְּאִלּוּ אֵינוֹ רוֹאֵהוּ
sources.says: Rashi says it means pressing your eyes shut as if you do not see it.

sources.quote: לֹא תִרְאֶה אוֹתוֹ שֶׁתִּתְעַלֵּם מִמֶּנּוּ, זֶהוּ פְּשׁוּטוֹ. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ פְּעָמִים שֶׁאַתָּה מִתְעַלֵּם
sources.says: Rashi says the plain sense is 'do not see it and ignore it', but the sages said there are times you may ignore it.

sources.quote: הָיָה כֹּהֵן וְהִיא בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת, אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה זָקֵן וְאֵינָהּ לְפִי כְּבוֹדוֹ, אוֹ שֶׁהָיְתָה מְלָאכָה שֶׁלּוֹ מְרוּבָּה מִשֶּׁל חֲבֵירוֹ, לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר
sources.says: The Talmud gives the cases: a priest when the animal is in a graveyard, an old man for whom it is beneath his dignity, or when his own work is worth more.

22:5.headline: A man's 'gear' on a woman: clothes, or weapons?
22:5.body: כלי can mean clothing or tools. Rashi says the verse is about a woman dressing like a man to slip in among men. Onkelos translates 'a man's weapons', and in the Talmud Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says it means a woman should not go out to war with weapons.

sources.quote: שֶׁתְּהֵא דּוֹמָה לְאִישׁ, כְּדֵי שֶׁתֵּלֵךְ בֵּין הָאֲנָשִׁים, שֶׁאֵין זוֹ אֶלָּא לְשֵׁם נִאוּף
sources.says: Rashi says it means she should not look like a man so as to go among men, which is only for the sake of adultery.

sources.quote: לָא יְהֵי תִקּוּן זֵין דִּגְבַר עַל אִתְּתָא
sources.says: Onkelos translates: a man's weapons shall not be on a woman.

sources.quote: מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא תֵּצֵא אִשָּׁה בִּכְלֵי זַיִין לְמִלְחָמָה
sources.says: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov learns from this verse that a woman should not go out to war bearing weapons.

22:6.headline: 'If a nest is called before you' means it happens by chance
22:6.body: יקרא usually means 'is called'. Ibn Ezra and Rashbam say here it means 'happens to be', from מקרה, chance. Rashi draws the law: the rule is for a nest you come upon, not one you prepared.

sources.quote: יקרא. כמו נקרא נקראתי והם מגזרת מקרה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says יקרא is like 'I happened to be there', from the word מקרה, chance.

sources.quote: כי יקרא - יזדמן על ידי מקרה
sources.says: Rashbam says it means that it turns up by chance.

sources.quote: כי יקרא. פְּרָט לִמְזֻמָּן
sources.says: Rashi says the wording excludes a nest that is already prepared, that is, one you own.

22:8.headline: 'The faller' is named before he falls
22:8.body: The verse calls the person 'the one who falls' before anything has happened. Ibn Ezra says he is named for his end, as many words are. Rashi says this man was due to fall anyway, but his death should not come through you.

sources.quote: הנופל. נקרא על שם סופו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the one who falls is named for how he ends up.

sources.quote: רָאוּי זֶה לִפֹּל, וְאַעַ"פִּ כֵן לֹא תִתְגַּלְגֵּל מִיתָתוֹ עַל יָדְךָ
sources.says: Rashi says this man deserved to fall, yet his death should not be brought about through you.

22:9.headline: 'Become holy' here means 'become forbidden'
22:9.body: תקדש usually means 'become holy'. Rashi says it is a word for anything set apart from a person, for good as with a gift to the Temple, or for bad as with something forbidden. Chizkuni reads it as 'become mixed'.

sources.quote: כָּל דָּבָר הַנִּתְעָב עַל הָאָדָם, בֵּין לְשֶׁבַח כְּגוֹן הֶקְדֵּשׁ, בֵּין לִגְנַאי כְּגוֹן אִסּוּר, נוֹפֵל בּוֹ לְשׁוֹן קִדּוּשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says anything kept away from a person, for praise like a holy gift or for disgrace like a ban, can be called קדוש.

sources.quote: תקדש - תאסר כקדשים
sources.says: Rashbam says it means it becomes forbidden like holy things.

sources.quote: פן תקדש פן תתערב
sources.says: Chizkuni says פן תקדש means 'lest it become mixed'.

22:11.headline: Shaatnez read as three steps: combed, spun, twisted
22:11.body: Rashi says שעטנז means a mixture. The Mishnah splits the word into שוע (combed), טווי (spun) and נוז (twisted): only cloth made that way is forbidden. Another sage reads it as נלוז, one who turns his Father in heaven against him.

sources.quote: שעטנז. לְשׁוֹן עֵרוּב. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ פֵּרְשׁוּ — שׁוּעַ טָווּי וְנוּז
sources.says: Rashi says שעטנז means mixing, and the sages explained it as combed, spun and twisted.

sources.quote: אֵין אָסוּר מִשּׁוּם כִּלְאַיִם אֶלָּא טָווּי וְאָרוּג, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים כב) לֹא תִלְבַּשׁ שַׁעַטְנֵז, דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא שׁוּעַ טָווּי וָנוּז
sources.says: The Mishnah says only spun and woven fabric is forbidden, since שעטנז means something combed, spun and twisted.

sources.quote: נָלוֹז וּמֵלִּיז הוּא אֶת אָבִיו שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם עָלָיו
sources.says: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar reads it as one who is crooked and turns his Father in heaven against him.

22:17.headline: Spreading the cloth: a real sheet, or a figure of speech?
22:17.body: Rashi says this is a figure of speech: the facts will be made as clear as a clean cloth. In the Talmud, Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says the words mean what they say, a real cloth. Ramban agrees there is no need to read it as a figure.

sources.quote: הֲרֵי זֶה מָשָׁל, מְחֻוָּרִין הַדְּבָרִים כַּשִּׂמְלָה
sources.says: Rashi says this is a metaphor: the matter is made as clear as a cloth.

sources.quote: וּבוֹרְרִין אֶת הַדָּבָר כְּשִׂמְלָה חֲדָשָׁה. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: דְּבָרִים כִּכְתָבָן, שִׂמְלָה מַמָּשׁ
sources.says: The Talmud says witnesses come for each side and make the matter clear like a new cloth, while Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says the words are literal: a real cloth.

sources.quote: וְאֵין צֹרֶךְ, כִּי זֹאת לְפָנִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מַכְנִיסִין הֶחָתָן וְהַכַּלָּה לַחֻפָּה
sources.says: Ramban says there is no need for the metaphor, since it was the custom in Israel to bring the couple to the wedding canopy and check.

23:1.headline: Kanaf: a garment's corner, or what it hides
23:1.body: כנף usually means a wing or the corner of a garment. Maimonides, following Ibn Janah, says it can also mean something hidden, so the verse means 'he shall not uncover his father's private matter'.

sources.quote: אמר שהוא נאמר גם במשמעות של הסתר
sources.says: Maimonides cites Ibn Janah that the word is also used in the sense of hiding.

sources.quote: וממנו לדעתי "וְלֹא יְגַלֶּה כְּנַף אָבִיו" (דברים כג,א) – לא יגלה את סתר אביו
sources.says: Maimonides says this verse belongs to that sense: he shall not uncover what his father keeps hidden.

23:3.headline: Mamzer: the stranger his own family will not own
23:3.body: Ramban reads ממזר as a man made a stranger (זר) to his brothers, because his father will not acknowledge him for shame. He also cites the Jerusalem Talmud, which reads the word as מום זר, 'a strange blemish'.

sources.quote: מַמְזֵר, שֵׁם לְאִישׁ מוּזָר מֵאֶחָיו וְיוֹדְעָיו, שֶׁלֹּא יִוָּדַע מֵאַיִן בָּא
sources.says: Ramban says mamzer is a name for a man estranged from his brothers and acquaintances, whose origin is unknown.

sources.quote: הוּא יַרְחִיק אוֹתוֹ וְלֹא יוֹדֶה בּוֹ לְבָשְׁתּוֹ וְלִכְלִמָּתוֹ
sources.says: Ramban says the father keeps him at a distance and will not acknowledge him, out of shame.

sources.quote: אָמַר ר' אַבְהוּ מַהוּ מַמְזֵר מוּם זָר
sources.says: Ramban cites Rabbi Abahu: what is mamzer? A strange blemish.

sources.quote: אמר רבי אבהו מאי ממזר, מום זר
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya cites the same reading from the Jerusalem Talmud.

23:5.headline: 'Al devar': not only 'because', but 'over the scheme'
23:5.body: על דבר is the usual phrase for 'because of'. Rashi reads דבר here as 'counsel': they are kept out over the plan they made to lead Israel into sin.
