sources.quote: רבי עקיבא אומר שהיו שורפים בניהם של ישראל בכור של אש
sources.says: Chizkuni cites Rabbi Akiva that the Egyptians burned Israel's children in a furnace of fire.

4:22.headline: Why say 'I will not cross' after 'I will die'?
4:22.body: Moses says he will die here and will not cross the Jordan, but the dead do not cross rivers anyway. Rashi says it means even his bones would not be carried over.

sources.quote: מאחר שמת מהיכן יעבר? אלא אף עצמותי אינם עוברים
sources.says: Rashi asks how a dead man could cross, and answers that even his bones would not cross.

4:25.headline: A hidden date for the first exile
4:25.body: The sages counted the letters of ונושנתם, 'you grow old', as numbers and got 852, the years until exile. Rashi says God sent the exile two years early, so the threat of total destruction would not come true.

sources.quote: רמז להם שיגלו ממנה לסוף שמונה מאות וחמשים ושתים שנה כמנין
sources.says: Rashi says the word hints that they would be exiled after 852 years, the number value of its letters.

sources.quote: והקדים שתי שנים ל"ונושנתם", כדי שלא יתקים בהם כי אבד תאבדון
sources.says: Rashi says God brought the exile two years early so that 'you will surely perish' would not be fulfilled.

sources.quote: ועמד הבית ת"י שנה, טול מהם ארבעים שנה שבמדבר נשארו תת"ן
sources.says: Bahya does the count: 480 years from the Exodus to the Temple, plus the 410 years it stood, minus the 40 years in the desert, makes 850.

4:32.headline: From one end of the sky to the other: Adam's height
4:32.body: Rashi says the plain meaning of asking 'from one end of the heavens to the other' is to ask all creatures everywhere. He also brings a midrash that the first human was so tall he reached from the earth to the sky.

sources.quote: וגם שאל לכל הברואים אשר מקצה אל קצה, זהו פשוטו
sources.says: Rashi says the plain meaning is to ask all creatures from end to end.

sources.quote: מלמד על קומתו של אדם שהיתה מן הארץ עד השמים
sources.says: Rashi brings the midrash that Adam's height reached from the earth to the sky.

4:35.headline: Israel was shown that God is alone
4:35.body: אתה הראת means 'you were shown'. Rashi says that at Sinai God opened the seven heavens and the depths below, and the people saw that He is alone.

sources.quote: כשנתן הקב"ה את התורה פתח להם שבעה רקיעים
sources.says: Rashi says that when God gave the Torah He opened the seven heavens for them.

sources.quote: וראו שהוא יחידי, לכך נאמר "אתה הראת לדעת"
sources.says: Rashi says they saw that He is alone, which is why the verse says 'you were shown, to know'.

5:3.headline: 'Not with our fathers': the covenant was also with us
5:3.body: The verse says God made the covenant 'not with our fathers', though He surely did. Rashi and Ibn Ezra read it as 'not with our fathers alone', but with us, the people standing here, as well.

sources.quote: לא את אבתינו בִּלְבַד
sources.says: Rashi reads it as 'not with our fathers only'.

sources.quote: לא את אבותינו. לבדם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reads it as 'not with our fathers alone'.

5:12.headline: 'Keep' here, 'Remember' in Exodus: both said at once
5:12.body: The first telling of the commandments, in Exodus, says 'Remember the Sabbath', and this one says 'Keep'. Rashi says God spoke both words at once, in a single utterance heard as one.

sources.quote: שְׁנֵיהֶם בְּדִבּוּר אֶחָד וּבְתֵבָה אַחַת נֶאֶמְרוּ, וּבִשְׁמִיעָה אַחַת נִשְׁמְעוּ
sources.says: Rashi says 'remember' and 'keep' were both said in one utterance and one word, and heard in one hearing.

6:4.headline: "The Lord is one": alone now, or one for all someday?
6:4.body: Rashbam and Ibn Ezra read אחד as "alone": only He is our God. Rashi reads it as a hope: He is our God now, and one day all nations will call Him by one name.

sources.quote: ה' הוא לבדו אלהינו ואין לנו אלוה אחר עמו
sources.says: Rashbam says the Lord alone is our God and we have no other god with Him.

sources.quote: ונכפל כמו כן לומר אחד והטעם לבדו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says אחד here means alone.

sources.quote: ה' שֶׁהוּא אֱלֹהֵינוּ עַתָּה, וְלֹא אֱלֹהֵי הָאֻמּוֹת, הוּא עָתִיד לִהְיוֹת ה' אֶחָד
sources.says: Rashi says the Lord who is our God now, and not yet the nations' God, will in the future be one Lord for all.

6:5.headline: "All your heart": both your good and bad urges
6:5.body: Rashi says "with all your heart" means with both inclinations, the good and the bad. Chizkuni explains that לבבך, with two ב's, can be read as "your two hearts", while Ibn Ezra says the heart here is the mind.

sources.quote: בכל לבבך. בִּשְׁנֵי יְצָרֶיךָ
sources.says: Rashi says it means with both your inclinations.

sources.quote: לבך לא מצי למקרי אלא חד אבל לבבך מצי למקרי לבביך שני לבבות
sources.says: Chizkuni says לבך can only mean one heart, but לבבך can be read as two hearts.

sources.quote: הלב הוא הדעת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the heart is the mind.

6:5.headline: "All your soul": even if it costs your life
6:5.body: Rashi and Rashbam read "with all your soul" as loving God even if He takes your life. Ibn Ezra reads נפש as the part of a person that desires, so the verse asks for every desire too.

sources.quote: ובכל נפשך. אֲפִלּוּ הוּא נוֹטֵל אֶת נַפְשְׁךָ
sources.says: Rashi says it means even if He takes your life.

sources.quote: לפי פשוטו: אפילו נוטלין את נפשך, שהרי כבר אמר: בכל לבבך
sources.says: Rashbam says the plain sense is even if they take your life, since "heart" was already said.

sources.quote: נפשך. היא הרוח שבגוף והיא המתאו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says נפש is the spirit in the body that desires.

6:5.headline: "All your might": your money, or whatever God measures out
6:5.body: מאד normally means "very", so Ibn Ezra and Ramban read "love Him very, very much". Rashi and the sages read it as "with all your money", and Rashi adds a play on מדה, "measure": love God whatever He measures out to you, good or bad.

sources.quote: מאדך. מטעם מאד מאד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says מאדך comes from "very, very".

sources.quote: וְעַל דַּעַת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ (ברכות נד) בְּכָל מָמוֹנְךָ
sources.says: Ramban cites the sages that it means with all your money.

sources.quote: בְּכָל מִדָּה וּמִדָּה שֶׁמּוֹדֵד לְךָ, בֵּין בְּמִדָּה טוֹבָה בֵּין בְּמִדַּת פֻּרְעָנוּת
sources.says: Rashi says it also means with every measure God measures to you, good or punishing.

6:7.headline: Teach them so they are sharp in your mouth
6:7.body: ושננתם comes from the word for sharpening, as in חץ שנון, "a sharpened arrow". Rashi says the words should be so sharp in your mouth that you can answer any question at once.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן חִדּוּד הוּא, שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מְחֻדָּדִים בְּפִיךָ
sources.says: Rashi says it means sharpness, so the words will be sharp in your mouth.

sources.quote: ושננתם. מגזרת חץ שנון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word comes from "a sharpened arrow".

sources.quote: ושננתם - לשון חדוד, לפרשם היטב
sources.says: Rashbam says it means sharpness: explain them well.

6:7.headline: "Your children" includes your students
6:7.body: Rashi says "your children" here means students, since the Bible calls students sons. In the same way, a teacher is called a father.

sources.quote: אֵלּוּ הַתַּלְמִידִים, מָצִינוּ בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהַתַּלְמִידִים קְרוּייִם בָּנִים
sources.says: Rashi says these are the students, since students are everywhere called sons.

sources.quote: כָּךְ הָרַב קָרוּי אָב
sources.says: Rashi adds that the teacher is called a father.

6:13.headline: "Swear by His name": a command, or a careful permission?
6:13.body: Ramban says this does not command anyone to swear; it warns that if you swear, it must be only by God. Rashi says you may swear by His name only if you truly fear Him, because then you will be careful with oaths.

sources.quote: אֵינוֹ מִצְוָה שֶׁיִּשָּׁבַע, אֲבָל הוּא אַזְהָרָה כִּי בִּשְׁמוֹ בִּלְבַד תִּשָּׁבַע
sources.says: Ramban says it is not a command to swear, but a warning to swear only by His name.

sources.quote: אִם יֵשׁ בְּךָ כָּל הַמִּדּוֹת הַלָּלוּ, שֶׁאַתָּה יָרֵא אֶת שְׁמוֹ וְעוֹבֵד אוֹתוֹ, אָז בִּשְׁמוֹ תִּשָּׁבֵעַ
sources.says: Rashi says only if you fear His name and serve Him may you swear by His name.

6:18.headline: "The right and the good": going beyond what the law requires
6:18.body: Rashi says doing "the right and the good" means settling fairly and going beyond the strict letter of the law. Ramban explains why: no list of laws can cover every case, so this verse asks for goodness where the law is silent.

sources.quote: זוֹ פְשָׁרָה לִפְנִים מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין
sources.says: Rashi says it means compromise, going beyond the line of the law.

sources.quote: וְעַתָּה יֹאמַר גַּם בַּאֲשֶׁר לֹא צִוְּךָ תֵּן דַּעְתְּךָ לַעֲשׂוֹת הַטּוֹב וְהַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו
sources.says: Ramban says the verse adds: even where He did not command you, take care to do what is good and right in His eyes.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַזְכִּיר בַּתּוֹרָה כָּל הַנְהָגוֹת הָאָדָם עִם שְׁכֵנָיו וְרֵעָיו
sources.says: Ramban says this is because the Torah cannot mention every way a person deals with neighbors and friends.

7:2.headline: "Do not favor them": no praise, and no place to settle
7:2.body: תחנם can come from חן, "grace", or from חניה, "camping". Rashi gives both: do not praise their beauty, and do not give them a foothold in the land. Onkelos reads it as "do not pity them".

sources.quote: לֹא תִתֵּן לָהֶם חֵן, אָסוּר לוֹ לָאָדָם לוֹמַר "כַּמָּה נָאֶה גוֹי זֶה". דָּבָר אַחֵר, לֹא תִּתֵּן לָהֶם חֲנִיָּה בָּאָרֶץ
sources.says: Rashi says it means do not give them grace, such as saying how handsome one of them is, or else do not give them a place to settle in the land.

sources.quote: לֹא תִּתֵּן לָהֶם חֲנָיָיה בַּקַּרְקַע. הַאי ״לָא תְחׇנֵּם״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ, דְּהָכִי קָאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא: לֹא תִּתֵּן לָהֶם חֵן
sources.says: The Talmud reads it as "do not give them a foothold in the land" and also brings the reading "do not give them grace".

sources.quote: וְלָא תְרַחַם עֲלֵיהוֹן
sources.says: Onkelos translates: and do not have mercy on them.

7:4.headline: Your daughter's child is still called "your son"
7:4.body: The verse warns that a foreign son-in-law will turn "your son" away from God. Rashi notes the child meant is your daughter's son, and learns that a daughter's child counts as yours, while a son's child by a foreign woman does not.

sources.quote: לִמְּדָנוּ שֶׁבֶּן בִּתְּךָ הַבָּא מִן הַגּוֹי קָרוּי בִּנְךָ, אֲבָל בֶּן בִּנְךָ הַבָּא מִן הַגּוֹיָה אֵינוֹ קָרוּי בִּנְךָ אֶלָּא בְּנָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says we learn that your daughter's son by a gentile is called your son, but your son's son by a gentile woman is called her son, not yours.

7:7.headline: "The fewest" also means "the ones who make themselves small"
7:7.body: Plainly, God chose Israel though they were the fewest of nations. Rashi brings a midrash: המעט means those who make themselves small, like Abraham saying "I am dust and ashes".

sources.quote: הַמְמַעֲטִין עַצְמְכֶם, כְּגוֹן אַבְרָהָם שֶׁאָמַר (בראשית י"ח) "וְאָנֹכִי עָפָר וָאֵפֶר"
sources.says: Rashi says it means you make yourselves small, like Abraham who said "I am dust and ashes".

sources.quote: כִּפְשׁוּטוֹ; וּמִדְרָשׁוֹ לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אַתֶּם מַגְדִּילִים עַצְמְכֶם כְּשֶׁאֲנִי מַשְׁפִּיעַ לָכֶם טוֹבָה
sources.says: Rashi says the plain meaning stands, and the midrash reads it as: you do not make yourselves big when I give you good things.

7:9.headline: "A thousand" generations here, "thousands" elsewhere
7:9.body: Here God keeps faith "to a thousand generations"; in the Ten Commandments it says "thousands". Rashi says "thousand" goes with those who keep His commands out of fear, and "thousands" with those who love Him.

sources.quote: כָּאן שֶׁהוּא סָמוּךְ אֵצֶל לְשֹׁמְרֵי מִצְוֹתָיו, הוּא אוֹמֵר לאלף, וּלְהַלָּן שֶׁהוּא סָמוּךְ אֵצֶל לְאֹהֲבַי, הוּא אוֹמֵר לַאֲלָפִים
sources.says: Rashi says it says "thousand" here next to "those who keep His commands" and "thousands" there next to "those who love Me".

sources.quote: ולשמרי מצותיו. אֵלּוּ הָעוֹשִׂין מִיִּרְאָה
sources.says: Rashi says those who keep His commands are those who act out of fear.

sources.quote: לאהביו. אֵלּוּ הָעוֹשִׂין מֵאַהֲבָה
sources.says: Rashi says those who love Him are those who act out of love.

7:10.headline: Repaid "to his face": now, so nothing is left for later
7:10.body: God repays His enemies "to his face". Rashi reads it as "in his lifetime": God pays the wicked for their good deeds now, to cut them off from the world to come. Ibn Ezra reads it as "to him himself".

sources.quote: בְּחַיָּיו מְשַׁלֵּם לוֹ גְמוּלוֹ הַטּוֹב, כְּדֵי לְהַאֲבִידוֹ מִן הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
sources.says: Rashi says God pays him his good reward in his lifetime, in order to destroy him from the world to come.

sources.quote: אל פניו. הטעם לעצמו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says "to his face" means to the person himself.

7:11.headline: Today is for doing; the reward comes tomorrow
7:11.body: Moses commands the laws "today, to do them". Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi reads it closely: today is the time to do them, and tomorrow, in the world to come, is the time to be paid.

sources.quote: ״הַיּוֹם לַעֲשׂוֹתָם״ — וְלֹא לְמָחָר לַעֲשׂוֹתָם, ״הַיּוֹם לַעֲשׂוֹתָם״ — לְמָחָר לְקַבֵּל שְׂכָרָם
sources.says: The Talmud says: today to do them, not tomorrow; today to do them, and tomorrow to receive their reward.

sources.quote: וּלְמָחָר, לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, לִטֹּל שְׂכָרָם
sources.says: Rashi says tomorrow, in the world to come, is for receiving their reward.

7:12.headline: "Because" is also "heel": the small commands people trample
7:12.body: עקב here means "because" or "in return for", as Ramban and Onkelos read it. But it is also the word for "heel". Rashi reads it as the light commands people tread on with their heels. Rabbeinu Bahya says the bodily rewards promised here are the low reward, low like the heel.

sources.quote: אִם הַמִּצְווֹת קַלּוֹת שֶׁאָדָם דָּשׁ בַּעֲקֵבָיו תשמעון
sources.says: Rashi says it means: if you listen to the light commands that people trample with their heels.

sources.quote: טַעַם עֵקֶב, כְּמוֹ בַּעֲבוּר, וְכֵן עֵקֶב אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַע אַבְרָהָם בְּקֹלִי
sources.says: Ramban says עקב means "because", as in "because Abraham listened to My voice".

sources.quote: וִיהֵי חֳלַף דִּי תְקַבְּלוּן
sources.says: Onkelos translates: and it will be, in return for your accepting.

sources.quote: הוא השכר הקל והשפל שיש לאדם, כי כן העקב שפל הגוף
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says these bodily rewards are the light and low reward, as the heel is the lowest part of the body.

7:13.headline: Flocks named for making their owners rich
7:13.body: עשתרות is an odd word for flocks. Onkelos simply says "flocks". The sages hear מעשירות, "they make rich": the flocks are named for enriching their owners.

sources.quote: וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמָם עַשְׁתָּרוֹת? שֶׁמַּעֲשִׁירוֹת אֶת בַּעֲלֵיהֶן
sources.says: Rashi brings the rabbis: they are called עשתרות because they enrich their owners.

sources.quote: וְעֶדְרֵי עָנָךְ
sources.says: Onkelos translates it as "the flocks of your sheep".

7:17.headline: Here כי can only mean "perhaps"
7:17.body: כי usually means "when" or "because". Rashi says that here it must mean "perhaps": perhaps you will say they are too many to defeat. Only that reading fits the answer that follows, "do not fear them".

sources.quote: עַל כָּרְחֲךָ לְשׁוֹן דִּילְמָא הוּא, שֶׁמָּא תֹאמַר בִּלְבָבְךָ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵם רַבִּים לֹא אוּכַל לְהוֹרִישָׁם, אַל תֹּאמַר כֵּן
sources.says: Rashi says it must mean "perhaps": perhaps you will say they are too many to drive out; do not say so.

7:20.headline: A hornet, a disease, or a word for shrinking?
7:20.body: God will send הצרעה against the hidden enemies. Rashi says it was a flying insect that shot venom and blinded them. Ibn Ezra reads it as a disease, from צרעת. Bekhor Shor reads it as "making small", with two letters swapped.

sources.quote: מִין שֶׁרֶץ הָעוֹף שֶׁהָיְתָה זוֹרֶקֶת בָּהֶם מָרָה וּמְסָרַסְתָּן וּמְסַמְּאָה אֶת עֵינֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it was a kind of flying insect that shot venom at them and blinded their eyes.

sources.quote: הצרעה. חולי בגוף מגזרת צרעת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is a bodily disease, from the word for leprosy.

sources.quote: ולפי הפשט נרא' צרעה צעירה כמו שמלה שלמה, כבשים כשבים, כלומ' שיצער וימעיט אותם
sources.says: Bekhor Shor says by the plain sense צרעה stands for צעירה with letters swapped, meaning God will make them small and few.

8:1.headline: 'The whole commandment': finish what you start
8:1.body: The verse says 'all the commandment', in the singular. A midrash in Rashi reads it as: if you began a good deed, finish it, because it is named after the one who completes it.

sources.quote: אם התחלת במצוה גמר אותה, שאינה נקראת אלא על שם הגומרה
sources.says: Rashi says if you started a commandment, finish it, since it is called by the name of the one who finishes it.

8:2.headline: Why would God need to test, if He already knows?
8:2.body: The verse says God tested Israel 'to know what is in your heart'. Chizkuni says God needs no test, since all is open to Him. Maimonides says 'to know' here means so that the nations would know that God feeds those who serve Him.

sources.quote: אין נסיון גבי הקב"ה שהרי הכל גלוי לפניו
sources.says: Chizkuni says there is no testing for God, since everything is revealed before Him.

sources.quote: כדי שידעו זאת האומות, ויפורסם בעולם שמי שמתמסר לעבודתו יתעלה, ה' יפרנס אותו ממקור שאינו עולה על הדעת
sources.says: Maimonides says it was so the nations would know that God feeds whoever gives himself to His service, from a source no one would imagine.

8:3.headline: How could manna make people hungry?
8:3.body: God gave food from heaven, yet the verse says He 'made you hungry'. Chizkuni gives two answers: manna came only one day at a time, and God let them run out of food first so they would accept a food they did not know.

sources.quote: שלא נתן לך מן אלא דבר יום ביומו וזהו וירעבך
sources.says: Chizkuni says God gave manna only day by day, and that is the hunger.

sources.quote: שאם הוריד לך מן בעוד שהיית שבע מן הצידה שהיתה בידך שהוצאת ממצרים לא היית משגיח עליו
sources.says: Chizkuni says had manna come while they were still full from food brought out of Egypt, they would not have paid attention to it.

8:9.headline: 'Its stones are iron' read as 'its builders are iron'
8:9.body: The Talmud reads אבניה, its stones, as בוניה, its builders, meaning its scholars. A true scholar must be firm as iron. Ravina adds that he must still teach himself to be gentle.

sources.quote: ארץ אשר אבניה ברזל״, אל תקרי ״אבניה״, אלא בוניה
sources.says: The Talmud says: do not read 'its stones' but 'its builders'.

sources.quote: כל תלמיד חכם שאינו קשה כברזל — אינו תלמיד חכם
sources.says: Rav Ashi says any scholar who is not hard as iron is not a scholar.

sources.quote: מיבעי ליה לאיניש למילף נפשיה בניחותא
sources.says: Ravina says a person must still train himself to be gentle.

8:10.headline: The one place the Torah commands us to bless God
8:10.body: The sages learned grace after meals from this word. Bahya notes this is the only place in the Torah where God commands people to bless Him.

sources.quote: ורבותינו (ברכות מח) קבלו שזו מצות עשה
sources.says: Ramban says the sages received that this is a positive commandment.

sources.quote: ולא תמצא בכל התורה בשום מקום שצוה הקב"ה שנברך לשמו כי אם במקום הזה
sources.says: Bahya says nowhere else in the Torah does God command us to bless His name.

8:20.headline: The section ends with the word it began with
8:20.body: The section opened 'because, עקב, you listen' (7:12) and closes 'because, עקב, you did not listen'. Rashbam says this closes the frame: listen and inherit, refuse and be lost.

sources.quote: זהו סיום כל תחילת הפרשה
sources.says: Rashbam says this is the close of the whole opening of the section.

sources.quote: והיה עקב תשמעון - תנחלו את הארץ - ועקב לא תשמעון - תאבדון ממנה
sources.says: Rashbam says if you listen you inherit the land, and if you do not you will be lost from it.

9:5.headline: Here כי means 'but', not 'because'
9:5.body: כי usually means 'because' or 'that'. Rashi says here it means 'but': not for your goodness, but because of these nations' wickedness.

sources.quote: הרי כי משמש בלשון אלא
sources.says: Rashi says כי here serves as the word 'but'.

9:20.headline: Aaron's 'destruction' meant losing his sons
9:20.body: Rashi says to destroy here means losing one's children, as in Amos 'I destroyed his fruit'. Moses' prayer helped half: two of Aaron's sons died and two lived.

sources.quote: זה כלוי בנים, וכן הוא אומר (עמוס ב') ואשמיד פריו ממעל
sources.says: Rashi says this means the loss of children, as Amos says 'I destroyed his fruit above'.

sources.quote: והועילה תפלתי לכפר מחצה, ומתו שנים ונשארו השנים
sources.says: Rashi says Moses' prayer atoned for half: two sons died and two remained.
